title: fix: transform pcb_solder_paste and other component-attached elements in transformPCBElement
description: Fixes the issue where solder paste and other component-attached elements were not transformed during PCB layout adjustments, leading to misalignment with their corresponding pads.
body:
Fixes the root cause of tscircuit/core#2897 (grid/array layout repositions pads without transforming their solder paste).

## Root cause

`repositionPcbComponentTo` selects elements to move by `pcb_component_id` / `pcb_port_id` membership and hands them to `transformPCBElements`. But `transformPCBElement` had no branch for `pcb_solder_paste` (and a few other component-attached geometric types), so those elements were selected for the move and then silently returned untransformed — left at their pre-layout coordinates.

This is why core's grid layout (which routes through `repositionPcbComponentTo`) leaves paste behind while core's own `_setPositionFromLayout` / `_moveCircuitJsonElements` paths (which translate paste explicitly core-side) do not.

## What this changes

Adds the missing branches, matching the existing handling patterns:

| type | fields transformed | pattern matched |
|---|---|---|
| `pcb_solder_paste` | `x`/`y`, rect `width`/`height` swap on quarter-turns | same as `pcb_smtpad` |
| `pcb_copper_text` | `anchor_position` | same as `pcb_silkscreen_text` |
| `pcb_trace_hint` | `route` points | same as `pcb_trace` |
| `pcb_silkscreen_pill` / `pcb_silkscreen_oval` | `center` | same as `pcb_silkscreen_rect` |

These are the geometric types that carry `pcb_component_id` in circuit-json and are emitted by core today (paste from `SmtPad`, copper text from `CopperText`, hints from `TraceHint`); the remaining unhandled types are error/warning records with no geometry to move.

## Verification

- New tests fail on `main` (6 failures), pass with the fix; full suite 97/97.
- Reproduced tscircuit/core#2897 on core `main` (4 grid-arranged 0402s → all 8 pastes at pre-layout positions, 3.28 mm/2.82 mm displacement), then re-ran with this branch's build linked in: every paste lands exactly on its pad (Δ = 0.000 mm). Core needs no change of its own — just the dependency bump once this releases.
- `bun test`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run format:check` all pass. (`package.json` is reformatted here because format-check was failing on `main` itself; drop that commit hunk if you'd rather keep it.)

title: feat: add fanout boundary padding props
description: Add reusable FanoutBoundaryPadding supporting scalar distance or directional distances for fanout boundary padding in autorouting and breakout components.
body:
## Summary

- add reusable `FanoutBoundaryPadding` supporting a scalar distance or directional `{ top, right, bottom, left }` distances
- expose `fanoutBoundaryPadding` on both `<breakout>` and `<autoroutingphase>`
- normalize distance strings to millimeters and reject negative padding
- export the shared type and schema from `@tscircuit/props`

## Motivation

The fanout solver needs a shared boundary around only the source footprint pads. Existing breakout `padding` controls the group/layout bounds around every child, so nearby destination footprints such as decoupling capacitors enlarge that boundary. This prop lets core/solver integration terminate fanout before those surrounding parts while leaving ordinary breakout layout padding unchanged.

Directional fields allow asymmetric escape room. Omitted directional values are defined as zero. When the prop is absent, downstream implementations can retain automatic pitch-based boundary inference.

## Proposed integration semantics

A subsequent fanout-solver/core change will resolve this padding against the union of source-pad bounds and pass the resulting shared boundary to the solver. When both are supplied, phase-level padding should override the breakout-level value.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 393 passed
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run check-circular-deps`
- `git diff --check`

title: Add via-in-pad autorouter opt-in
description: Adds an option to the autorouter configuration to allow via-in-pad routing, which is disabled by default, and updates the documentation accordingly.
body:
## Summary

- add `allowViaInPad?: boolean` to `AutorouterConfig`
- validate the option through the public autorouter Zod schema
- document that omitted or `false` keeps via-in-pad routing disabled
- regenerate the component-types and props-overview documentation

## Why

Via-in-pad manufacturing can incur additional fabrication cost, so it should be an explicit autorouter opt-in. This props change establishes the user-facing API for the downstream Circuit JSON, core, and capacity-autorouter integrations.

This PR only introduces the props contract; it does not enable via-in-pad routing by itself.

description: Add signed thermalpadcenteroffsetx and thermalpadcenteroffsety parameters to QFNDFNSOICTSSOPSSOPMSOPVSSOP footprints, allowing for offset thermal pads while preserving existing footprints with default values of zero.
body:
## Summary

- add signed `thermalpadcenteroffsetx` and `thermalpadcenteroffsety` parameters to QFN/DFN/SOIC/TSSOP/SSOP/MSOP/VSSOP footprints
- keep both offsets at zero by default, preserving existing footprints
- include offset thermal pads in quad-family courtyard bounds

Several common JLCPCB power packages use an exposed pad that is intentionally displaced from the perimeter-pad center. A centered-only thermal pad caps otherwise accurate matches around 80–86% copper IoU.

This enables strings such as:

`dfn8_thermalpad2.4mmx2.1mm_thermalpadcenteroffsety0.35mm`

title: feat: apply fanout boundary padding
description: Adds fanout boundary padding control to the autorouting phase, allowing for more precise routing around components and obstacles.
body:
## Summary

- carry `fanoutBoundaryPadding` through routing phase plans and local autorouter strategy context
- use `<autoroutingphase>` padding in preference to containing `<breakout>` padding
- resolve the fanout solver's `sharedBoundary` from the union of source pad obstacles only
- support scalar and directional padding, rotated pads, and multiple source footprints
- preserve the solver's existing automatic pitch-based boundary inference when the prop is omitted
- update PCB and multi-stage autorouting snapshots for the BGA-plus-decoupling-caps and directed fanout cases

## Behavior

`padding` continues to control breakout layout bounds. `fanoutBoundaryPadding` controls where fanout prefixes terminate. Nearby destination parts and component keepouts do not enlarge the fanout boundary; the downstream autorouter continues from that boundary to the destinations.

When a phase supplies `fanoutBoundaryPadding`, it overrides the containing breakout value for that phase.

## Dependency

This uses `@tscircuit/props@^0.0.598`. [tscircuit/props#764](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/764) is merged, `0.0.598` is published, and the installed npm artifact exports the `FanoutBoundaryPadding` type, schema, and component props.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 1,277 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- targeted fanout, single-layer fanout, BGA breakout, strategy, preset, and shared-boundary tests
- visually inspected the updated BGA breakout PNG; fanout prefixes end around the BGA and downstream routes continue to the four capacitors
- `git diff --check`

title: feat: add single-layer and multilayer fanout autorouters
description: Add single-layer and multilayer fanout autorouters to the autorouting system, allowing for improved routing strategies and flexibility in PCB design.
body:
## Summary

- add `autorouter="single_layer_fanout"` and `autorouter="fanout"`
- register both modes through the local-autorouter strategy extension point now on `main`
- run `@tscircuit/fanout-solver` as a breakout-only stage that returns escape traces plus a transformed SimpleRouteJson
- pass that transformed problem to a separate default-autorouter follow-up stage
- read per-bus fanout policy from `<autoroutingphase busFanoutDirections={...}>`
- infer the source footprint without requiring a component selector
- preserve circular pad geometry for interstitial and thermal-pad escapes
- replace escaped source pads with fixed source-footprint keepouts for downstream routing
- keep `<bus>` limited to electrical connection membership
- bundle the fanout solver into core

## Integration cleanup

- rebased onto `main` after tscircuit/props#761 and tscircuit/core#2898 merged
- reduced the PR to one fanout feature commit
- updated to `@tscircuit/props@0.0.595`
- made `Breakout` parse its runtime props with `breakoutProps`, so the schema-owned `autorouter="fanout"` default is honored without duplicating it in the constructor
- kept concrete autorouter selection in the strategy registry and simplified the multi-stage SimpleRouteJson handoff in `Group`

## Breakout coverage

- two-layer `<breakout>` regression with a 6×6, 0.8 mm-pitch BGA surrounded on four sides by four 0603 decoupling capacitors
- four two-signal buses
- fanout phase produces eight boundary escape traces and eight vias
- downstream phase completes all 16 trace segments to the capacitors
- no PCB autorouting, trace-clearance, pad-clearance, or via-clearance errors under 0.1 mm trace/clearance rules and 0.2/0.5 mm via geometry
- full PCB and multi-stage SimpleRouteJson snapshots

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused fanout, breakout, bus, and preset tests
- full local suite: 1,276 passing, 31 skipped, 0 failing
- `git diff --check`
- PCB and phase-stack snapshots visually verified: fanout stops at the shared breakout boundary, then the default stage completes routing to the surrounding capacitors

title: refactor: extract local autorouter strategies
description: Refactors the autorouting system by extracting local autorouter strategies from Group.ts, introducing a strategy interface for router creation and cache policy, while maintaining existing behavior and ensuring the default strategy remains cacheable.
body:
## Summary

- move default local-autorouter construction out of `Group.ts`
- introduce a small strategy interface for router creation and cache policy
- keep the strategy registry empty so every current preset follows the unchanged default path
- add a focused regression proving the default strategy remains cacheable and constructs `TscircuitAutorouter` with the original SimpleRouteJson

This is deliberately behavior-neutral. It creates the extension point needed by specialized autorouters without including fanout presets, fanout dependencies, multi-stage routing, or breakout behavior.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- focused autorouter tests: 3 passing, 0 failing
- `git diff --check`
- all GitHub test, type-check, format, smoke-test, and Vercel checks passing

title: Use optimized DRC engine for autorouting repair
description: Updates Pipeline 7 to use an optimized DRC engine for autorouting repair, improving evaluation speed and efficiency by reusing DRC state and focusing on changing route geometry.
body:
## Summary

- update `high-density-repair03` to the commit that introduces `AutoroutingDrcEngine`
- route Pipeline 7's exact-geometry repair candidate scoring through a reusable optimized DRC engine
- preserve `@tscircuit/checks` as the reference/debug/benchmark evaluator, outside the autorouting hot path
- add focused parity coverage for Pipeline 7 trace-collision detection

## Why

Pipeline 7 currently supplies a custom relaxed DRC evaluator backed by `@tscircuit/checks`. That converts every repair candidate to Circuit JSON and reruns the general-purpose checks suite, bypassing the optimized engine and making repeated autorouting repair evaluations unnecessarily slow.

The new adapter compiles the static SRJ geometry and connectivity once, keeps Pipeline 7's final-output route conversion rules, and evaluates only changing route geometry on each candidate.

## Dependency

This is stacked on https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/34 and temporarily pins its exact feature commit (`5a963f132a640b38ec75d3ea2f72af2125636d3b`). The pin should be updated to the merged canonical commit before this PR lands.

## Validation

- `bun run build`
- `bun test tests/pipeline7-autorouting-drc-evaluator.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bun test tests/pipeline7-relaxed-drc-evaluator.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bun test tests/features/never-fail-growth-high-density/pipeline7-integration.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bun test tests/features/via-in-pad-opt-in.test.ts --timeout 9999999`

The broader local suite was stopped at the request of the author; GitHub CI is the remaining validation source. No benchmark was run locally.

title: Support immutable routes during trace simplification
description: Add an optional otherHdRoutes input to TraceSimplificationSolver to allow immutable routes to participate in collision checks without being modified, enabling better handling of preloaded traces during simplification.
body:
## Summary

- add an optional `otherHdRoutes` input to `TraceSimplificationSolver`
- propagate immutable peer routes through via removal, same-net via merging, and path simplification
- include immutable routes in collision indexes without adding them to mutation queues or solver output
- resolve synthetic peer-route connectivity through `rootConnectionName`
- render immutable peers as subdued, dashed layer-colored traces and cover the result with an SVG snapshot

## Why

A simplifier sometimes needs to avoid copper that is already routed but must not modify it. Previously the only way for a route to participate in simplification collision checks was to include it in the editable route list. Pipeline9 exposed this gap for preloaded traces, but this change is generic and has no Pipeline9 dependency.

This is the first independently mergeable prerequisite extracted from #1755.

## Validation

### Motivation

Provide a minimal Matchpack reproduction for a Core schematic containing an SOIC-16 chip and a directly connected 0402 resistor. Core emits the visually horizontal resistor with X-axis pin offsets, a taller reserved bounding box, and a 180° rotation, demonstrating why neither rotation nor reserved dimensions alone identify its orientation.

### Reproduction

- Runs the captured input through `LayoutPipelineSolver`.

### Evidence

Current Core solves the captured input with `R1` at `(-1.6, 0.7)`. Unmodified Matchpack `main` reproduces the problematic offset and places `R1` at `(-1.6, 0.5)`, rotation 180°, in 72 iterations.

title: Fix schematic testpoint overlaps with collision-aware body and trace search
description: Fixes schematic testpoint overlaps by implementing a collision-aware placement algorithm that ensures testpoints are positioned clear of nearby component bodies and connection traces.
body: ### Motivation Anchored schematic testpoints could be moved clear of nearby component bodies while their straight pin-to-pin connection traces still crossed components such as `SW_RESET` and `C_EN`. The scattered-testpoint reproduction therefore remained visually invalid even after basic body-overlap handling. Before: After: ### Change `AlignTestPointsSolver` now performs a two-stage, rotation-aware placement search: - move the complete ordered testpoint group outward until every testpoint body has `chipGap` clearance - search nearest tangent-axis offsets while preserving group order, rotation, and spacing - reject candidates whose testpoint bodies overlap another component - score each valid candidate using absolute testpoint-pin and anchor-pin positions - select the nearest candidate with the fewest connection-segment intersections - derive the search boundary from the actual component and group extents The solver exposes the final connection-body crossing count so regressions can assert geometric correctness directly. ### Evidence - the blocker regression verifies body clearance and zero connection crossings - the scattered-testpoint reproduction now reports zero component overlaps - the same reproduction reports zero connection-body crossings - the updated SVG snapshot shows both testpoint bodies and connection traces clear of nearby components

title: Prevent traces from using narrow component text gaps
description: Fixes routing behavior by treating sub-minimum gaps between a component and its attached text as closed routing channels, ensuring accurate trace routing.
body: ## Summary - treat sub-minimum gaps between a component and its attached text as closed routing channels - use the shared `Bounds` type and `boundsDistance` from `@tscircuit/math-utils` - allow endpoint-text detours for both same-chip and cross-chip traces - add the core-captured `U1.pin5 -> R1.pin1` repro alongside the existing same-chip repro - add a focused obstacle-boundary unit test ## Root cause The obstacle model treated the chip body and its attached MPN text as unrelated rectangles. Core places that text 0.04 schematic units from the chip, so a zero-width mathematical trace centerline could use the gap even though the rendered route should not. The prior fix incorrectly classified this by connection topology. The solver now uses `boundsDistance` to close only chip-to-attached-text gaps narrower than the 0.05 minimum routable gap. title: Fix labeled peripheral traces dropped by distance and routing failures
description: Fixes the issue where explicit labeled connections to single-pin peripherals disappear when their distance exceeds the maximum allowed distance during routing attempts.
body:
### Motivation

Explicit labeled connections to single-pin peripherals could disappear when their straight-line distance exceeded `maxMspPairDistance`. Some were skipped during MSP pairing, while others entered MSP pairing but disappeared after the first collision-free routing attempt failed.

The included bug report reproduces three missing connections:

- `schematic_port_3` to `schematic_port_56` (`IO4` to `TCH1`)
- `schematic_port_4` to `schematic_port_57` (`IO5` to `TCH2`)
- `schematic_port_7` to `schematic_port_60` (`IO15` to `TCH5`)

### Change

- Recognize explicit labeled connections between horizontally opposing pins when one endpoint belongs to a single-pin peripheral.
- Keep those connections in `MspConnectionPairSolver` even when they exceed the normal distance cutoff.
- Pass failed MSP pairs to `LongDistancePairSolver` and retry the labeled peripheral subset before generating fallback candidates.
- Reuse each failed pair and its existing `mspPairId`; the retry path does not synthesize identifiers.
- Preserve the existing distance and collision behavior for other connection shapes.

### Evidence

- Added regression assertions that all three previously missing pin pairs remain in the final routed trace set.
- Updated the bug-report schematic snapshot.
- No unrelated snapshots changed.

### Tests

- `bun test tests/bug-reports/bug-report-20260728T225606Z/bug-report-20260728T225606Z.test.ts`

title: Clear copper around pill-shaped plated holes
description: Fixes copper pour issues by converting pill-shaped plated holes into pill obstacles, ensuring proper clearance and eliminating shorts in the Gerber output.
body:
## What changed

- convert pill-shaped `pcb_plated_hole` elements into pill obstacles using their outer dimensions and rotation
- extend the pill-pad regression with the USB-C shield plated-hole geometry from `rp2040-motor-controller`
- update the SVG snapshot to cover the resulting clearance cutout

## Root cause

The Circuit JSON adapter handled circular plated holes and circular holes with rectangular pads, but silently omitted plated holes whose `shape` is `pill`. Copper pours therefore crossed USB-C shield plated holes even when those holes belonged to a different connectivity group.

## Impact

On the current `tscircuit/rp2040-motor-controller` build, `tsci check shorts` reported 24 Gerber-mode shorts. Re-solving the board with this patch removes all 20 copper-pour/plated-hole contacts; the four remaining reports are unrelated unconnected DRV8833 thermal vias (`pcb_via_0..3`) overlapping the exposed GND pad.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun test` — 35 passing
- `bun run build`
- real-board Gerber verification: 24 shorts before, 4 non-pour shorts after

body:
## Summary

- add a reusable `AutoroutingDrcEngine` that evaluates native simplified traces and SRJ obstacles without rebuilding Circuit JSON for every candidate
- compile static obstacle/connectivity data once and use layer-aware spatial hashes for trace/trace, trace/via, trace/pad, plated-hole, and via/via checks
- reuse the engine across `GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver` and `GlobalDrcBranchPortfolioSolver` candidate evaluations
- preserve custom `drcEvaluator` precedence and keep the `@tscircuit/checks` fallback for direct benchmark/debug/reference snapshots
- export the engine and its public types, document the intended autorouting-only boundary, and add parity, connectivity, edge-case, broad-phase, and randomized differential tests

## Why

Candidate scoring currently converts routes to Circuit JSON and reconstructs connectivity/spatial state for every repair attempt. That correctness-oriented path is useful for final validation and debugging, but it is expensive inside the autorouting search loop. This change introduces a focused evaluator for the relaxed autorouting objective while retaining `@tscircuit/checks` as the independent reference path.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 49 tests passed, 382 assertions
- `bun run formatcheck`
- 100 deterministic randomized geometry cases: the optimized engine missed zero error IDs reported by the reference checks
- full 44-sample DRC14 benchmark: identical final reference result to canonical `main` (76 initial errors, 3 final errors, 41/44 clean)
- same DRC14 harness/runtime environment: total solve time decreased from about 9.30s on canonical `main` to 6.23s on this branch (~33% reduction)
- 500-trace synthetic hot-path comparison: approximately 8.4x faster than repeated Circuit JSON conversion plus `@tscircuit/checks`

## Correctness boundary

This is intentionally an autorouting candidate-scoring engine, not a replacement for full-board DRC. Direct snapshots without an engine continue to use `@tscircuit/checks`. Across the 44 raw DRC14 evaluator inputs, error IDs matched exactly on 42 samples; on the remaining two, the optimized engine conservatively reported one additional geometric trace-to-pad finding and did not miss a reference error. End-to-end final reference outcomes remained identical to `main`.

title: Minimize Runtime Image by Isolating Production Dependencies
description: Optimizes the production container by introducing a dedicated production dependency stage and moving buildUI-only packages into devDependencies.
body:
This PR optimizes the production container by introducing a dedicated production dependency stage and moving build/UI-only packages into `devDependencies`.

### Changes

* Add a `production-dependencies` Docker stage that installs only production dependencies.
* Copy runtime `node_modules` from the production stage instead of the build stage.
* Reclassify frontend, UI, and build-time libraries as `devDependencies`.
* Keep only runtime-required packages in `dependencies`.

### Benefits

* Significantly reduces the final Docker image size.
* Eliminates unnecessary development dependencies from production.
* Decreases the runtime attack surface.
* Produces a cleaner separation between build-time and runtime requirements.
* Improves container startup and deployment efficiency.

title: Route clad1 RP2040 fanout on one layer
description: Routes all 132 connections of the clad1 RP2040 on a single top copper layer using an adaptive exit pass after push-and-shove fails, addressing clearance conflicts and improving routing efficiency.
body:
## Summary

- add an opt-in adaptive single-layer exit pass after push-and-shove fails
- route the complete 132-connection clad1 RP2040 reproduction on top copper
- key copper clearance by canonical connectivity nets and locally merge enclosed same-net terminals
- allow the global pass to select alternate shared-boundary sides when preferred exits would cross
- make adaptive-router debug logging safe in browser/Cosmos runtimes
- update Dataset 06, its rendered result, documentation, and regression coverage

## Root cause

The serialized board assigns multiple `source_trace_*` connection names to the same canonical `connectivity_net*`. Treating those names as different nets created false clearance conflicts. The exposed RP2040 pad is also enclosed and must join a same-net perimeter escape, while forcing all original outward exit preferences creates unavoidable single-layer crossings.

The first adaptive-router version also read `process.env.FANOUT_FLOW_DEBUG` directly. Cosmos runs in a browser where `process` is undefined, so clicking Solve raised a `ReferenceError`. The debug flag now uses an optional `globalThis.process` lookup and remains disabled in browser builds.

## Impact

Dataset 06 now routes all 132 connections on one top-copper layer using 0.1 mm trace width and 0.1 mm clearance. Every committed route terminates on the shared boundary and uses only straight or 45-degree segments.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 22 passed, 0 failed
- `bun test tests/dataset06-clad1-rp2040-repro.test.ts` — 279 assertions passed
- `bun run build:site` — Cosmos/Vite browser export succeeded

## Summary

- add a checked-in, deterministic dataset of 20 randomly generated boundary-routing problems
- scale both dimensions across five buckets: 20/8, 40/16, 60/24, 80/32, and 100/40 via/breakout ports
- increase routing demand from 4 to 20 two-terminal nets while preserving random reciprocal via pairings
- keep via and breakout ports on the top, right, and bottom boundaries
- add dataset regeneration, benchmark scripts, machine-readable/Markdown results, and structural/determinism tests
- document the benchmark workflow and current results

## Results

Measured with Bun 1.3.2 on macOS arm64 after one warm-up run. Successful-solve percentiles only include solved cases; attempt percentiles include every case.

| Via ports | Breakout ports | Solved | Solved p50 (ms) | Solved p95 (ms) | Attempt p50 (ms) | Attempt p95 (ms) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 20 | 8 | 3/4 (75%) | 0.88 | 1.82 | 1.40 | 5.12 |
| 40 | 16 | 2/4 (50%) | 6.41 | 8.52 | 11.49 | 22.35 |
| 60 | 24 | 0/4 (0%) | n/a | n/a | 102.65 | 188.31 |
| 80 | 32 | 0/4 (0%) | n/a | n/a | 217.69 | 944.56 |
| 100 | 40 | 0/4 (0%) | n/a | n/a | 360.17 | 821.48 |
| **Overall** | **8–40** | **5/20 (25%)** | **1.92** | **7.81** | **102.65** | **910.16** |

The corpus bounds each search at four blockers and 20,000 A* states, with eight rips per route and 100 total rips. At 24 or more breakout ports, sampled cases exhaust blocker or rip limits; their wall-clock costs remain included in attempt percentiles.

## Verification

- `bun run lint`

description: Summary Fixes tsci import RK3566, which successfully finds JLCPCB part C2943786 but fails during EasyEDA conversion.  Root Cause Search works correctly and resolves RK3566 to C2943786. They were interpreted as JavaScript scientific notation and converted to 100000000000000000000, resulting in invalid and duplicate generated port names. Result C2943786 now imports with: 565 unique footprint pads 565 unique generated ports Preserved BGA identifiers such as 1A1 and 1E20 Available CAD model A generic tscircuit fallback schematic  Tests Added coverage using the actual C2943786 EasyEDA payload: Focused tests for missing schematic metadata Regression test for preserving 1E20 Generated TSX inline snapshot PCB SVG snapshot Generated fallback schematic SVG snapshot 3D snapshot TypeScript, Biome, build, and snapshot tests pass.
body:
## Summary

Fixes `tsci import RK3566`, which successfully finds JLCPCB part `C2943786` but fails during EasyEDA conversion.

## Root Cause

Search works correctly and resolves `RK3566` to `C2943786`. The failure occurs during the subsequent import/conversion step.

EasyEDA returns this component as footprint-only data:

- `dataStr.shape` is explicitly empty, so no EasyEDA schematic symbol is available.
- `editorVersion`, `hasIdFlag`, `BBox`, and `colors` are omitted.
- `packageDetail` is complete and contains all 565 footprint pads.
- A CAD model is available.

Our Zod schema incorrectly required the omitted schematic metadata, causing validation to fail before footprint conversion.

There was also a separate parsing issue with BGA ball identifiers such as `1E20`. They were interpreted as JavaScript scientific notation and converted to `100000000000000000000`, resulting in invalid and duplicate generated port names.

## Solution

- Provide neutral defaults for optional schematic metadata:
  - `editorVersion: ""`
  - `hasIdFlag: false`
  - `colors: []`
  - A zero-size `BBox` positioned at the schematic origin
- Preserve exponent-like and alphanumeric BGA identifiers such as `1E20` as strings.
- Continue converting plain decimal pad identifiers to numbers to preserve existing behavior.

The fix does not add or reconstruct missing EasyEDA schematic data. It only allows footprint-only components to pass validation.

When the generated TSX is executed, tscircuit creates its existing generic chip schematic from the footprint pad identifiers. Therefore, the schematic snapshot represents the tscircuit-generated fallback, not an EasyEDA-provided RK3566 schematic.

## Result

`C2943786` now imports with:

- 565 unique footprint pads
- 565 unique generated ports
- Preserved BGA identifiers such as `1A1` and `1E20`
- Available CAD model
- A generic tscircuit fallback schematic

## Tests

Added coverage using the actual `C2943786` EasyEDA payload:

- Focused tests for missing schematic metadata
- Regression test for preserving `1E20`
- Generated TSX inline snapshot
- PCB SVG snapshot
- Generated fallback schematic SVG snapshot
- 3D snapshot

TypeScript, Biome, build, and snapshot tests pass.

title: fix: bump @tscircuit/circuit-json-util to 0.0.102 so PCB transforms (grid layout, subcircuit anchoring) move solder paste with pads
description: Fixes solder paste misalignment in grid layouts by updating the circuit-json-util dependency to ensure proper transformation of solder paste with pads.
body:
## What

Bumps `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` from `^0.0.101` to `^0.0.102` and adds a grid-layout regression test asserting every `pcb_solder_paste` stays centered on its pad.

## Why / Origin

Fixes #2897 (grid/array layout repositions pads without transforming their solder paste). The root cause was in circuit-json-util's `transformPCBElement`, which silently skipped `pcb_solder_paste` and other component-attached geometric elements — fixed upstream in tscircuit/circuit-json-util#110 and released in v0.0.102. Core's `^0.0.101` pin semver-excludes `0.0.102`, so the fix needs this explicit bump to reach grid layouts. Root-cause analysis is in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/2897#issuecomment-5108529394.

## Before / After

Before: a 2×2 `pcbGrid` of 0402s emits all 8 `pcb_solder_paste` records at pre-layout coordinates, up to 3.28 mm from their pads — stencil apertures land off-pad.
After: every paste aperture follows its pad exactly (Δ = 0.000 mm).

## Testing

- New `tests/features/grid/pcb-grid5-solder-paste.test.tsx` fails on `^0.0.101` (`Received: 3.28`) and passes with `0.0.102`.
- Ran the surrounding layout surface locally (grid, board-grid, panel grids, pcb-pack, flex, solder-paste creation tests): 44 pass / 0 fail, snapshots unchanged.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; biome format clean.

title: repro: solder jumper bridge trace disconnected endpoint false positive
description: Fixes false positive DRC error for solder jumper bridge traces due to missing connection metadata in the PCB rendering process.
body:
A minimal 2-pin `<solderjumper>` with `pw=0.6604` generates a false `pcb_trace_error`.

The bridge trace has `source_trace_id: undefined` — it is created by the footprinter without connection metadata. The DRC (`checkTracesAreContiguous`) cannot find a `source_trace` for it, so `expectedPorts` is empty and it falls to a geometry-based "any pad" check. Because the trace endpoint lands exactly at the pad edge (`padWidth/2` from center), IEEE 754 compound FP error (~5.55e-17mm) makes `isPointInPad` fail, falsely reporting "disconnected endpoint."

The PCB SVG renders correctly — the trace connects pad-to-pad visually.

**Root cause:** `SolderJumper.doInitialPcbPortAttachment()` in core does not create `source_trace` entries for bridge traces or set `source_trace_id` on their `pcb_trace` entries. Fix belongs in `lib/components/normal-components/SolderJumper.ts`.

title: Lay out parallel series branches
description: Detects and aligns strongly connected series paths to two pins on the same side of a main chip, introducing a new solver for parallel series branches while preserving component rotations and maintaining clearance.
body: ## Summary - detect even strong-connection series paths that leave and return to two pins on the same side of a main chip - add a dedicated `ParallelSeriesBranchSolver` inner-partition strategy that starts from the generic packed layout and folds matching paths into two aligned branches - preserve allowed component rotations and reject refinements that cannot maintain `chipGap` - add Core-captured BQ24074 repro coverage for both top-side and right-side chip pins ## Root cause The generic packer minimizes connection distance, but the affected topology has multiple compact foldings. It has no concept of the conventional U-shaped schematic arrangement, so one status LED branch could be placed in line with the other branch instead of forming two parallel columns or rows. The new behavior is isolated from `SingleInnerPartitionPackingSolver`: `PackInnerPartitionsSolver` selects the specialized strategy only when the topology matches, and the solver retains the original packed placement if the refinement is unsafe. ## Impact Strongly connected series branches now align predictably with the side of the main chip without manual `schX`/`schY` coordinates. Top/bottom attachments become parallel columns, while left/right attachments become parallel rows. ## Validation - `bun test` — 80 passed, 1 skipped - `bun run build` - `bun run format:check` - focused top-side and right-side BQ24074 repro tests and SVG snapshots Before: After:

## Summary

- add 16 deterministic SRJ18 repair fixtures captured at the real Pipeline7 → repair03 boundary
- make SRJ18 the default local and CI benchmark while retaining `--dataset drc14`
- generalize the benchmark runner, shell wrapper, workflow dispatch, and PR comment interface to select either dataset

## Why

Repair03 needs a benchmark that measures the solver on realistic autorouter output without rerunning the full autorouter or reconstructing routes from the original KiCad boards.

The checked-in fixtures capture the transformed SRJ scene, terminal-locked and width-adjusted HD routes, serializable solver settings, and provenance immediately before `GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver` takes its first step. They were generated from canonical `tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter@c5446f9b86efb32c3e033dada58635d7cbd95cd6` using `AutoroutingPipelineSolver7_MultiGraph`.

The fixtures are gzip-compressed to approximately 1.2 MB total and require no `dataset-srj18` or autorouter dependency during normal repair03 benchmarks.

## Impact

- `bun run benchmark`, `./benchmark.sh`, `/benchmark`, and automatic benchmark workflow runs now default to SRJ18
- DRC14 remains available through `--dataset drc14` or `bun run benchmark:drc14`
- manual workflow dispatch exposes a `drc14` / `srj18` dataset selector
- benchmark reports include the selected dataset and only calculate main-branch deltas for matching datasets

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test` — 49 passed
- `bun run formatcheck`
- `bash -n benchmark.sh`

- validated all 16 compressed fixture payloads and their provenance

The editor was developed against React 19 types, where mutable refs commonly include `null` in the generic type. React 18 models `RefObject` differently, so consumers compiling the package source received incompatible `LegacyRef<HTMLDivElement>` errors and a readonly `.current` assignment error.

Using a callback ref for the Radix menu item and a small mutable-ref contract for the Monaco editor avoids relying on version-specific React ref definitions.

## Summary

## Why

The package imports TypeScript at runtime for type acquisition, but declaring TypeScript 6 as a regular dependency forces consumers that use TypeScript 5 to install a second compiler copy. This can increase bundle size and create mismatched compiler API or AST behavior.

Making TypeScript a peer dependency lets the host application provide one compatible TypeScript installation while the editor retains TypeScript 6 for its own development and validation.

description: Adds a rotated_pill shape variant to pcb_solder_paste, allowing for a paste aperture that matches the pad outline exactly.

## What

Adds a `rotated_pill` shape variant to `pcb_solder_paste`, mirroring the existing `pcb_smtpad` `rotated_pill` variant (`width`, `height`, `radius`, `ccw_rotation`).

## Why

`pcb_smtpad` has had a `rotated_pill` variant for a while, but `pcb_solder_paste` only supports circle/rect/pill/rotated_rect/oval — the pill paste variant has no rotation field, so a rotated pill pad cannot get a same-shape paste aperture. This came up in tscircuit/core#2930 (review: the rotated-rect fallback there is a hack); with this variant core can emit a paste aperture that matches the pad outline exactly.

## Tests

title: feat: add solderPasteMargin prop to all smtpad variants
description: Adds solderPasteMargin prop to every smtpad shape variant, allowing for customizable solder paste aperture margins.
body:
## What

Adds **`solderPasteMargin?: Distance`** to every `<smtpad>` shape variant (rect, rotated_rect, circle, pill, polygon) — an absolute per-side margin for the solder paste aperture, mirroring the existing `solderMaskMargin` prop (positive grows the aperture, negative shrinks it).

## Why

`SmtPad.doInitialPcbPrimitiveRender()` in core shrinks every paste aperture to a hard-coded `0.7 ×` the pad dimensions (0.49 of the pad area). As measured in tscircuit/core#2896, that pushes fine-pitch/leadless packages (VQFN, WSON) below the IPC-7525 area-ratio release floor of 0.66, and there is currently no prop to say otherwise — manufacturers' own stencil drawings for those packages specify 1:1 apertures.

The prop is purely additive and optional; nothing changes for existing designs. The core-side change that consumes it (per-pad margin with the current `0.7` behaviour staying the default) is a follow-up PR in tscircuit/core.

## Tests

- `tests/smtpad.test.ts`: parses `solderPasteMargin` (mm-string and number, positive and negative) on all five shape variants, and checks it stays optional.

title: Make breakout a transparent routing directive
description: Removes forced subcircuit behavior from Breakout, allowing it to function as a transparent routing directive while maintaining board-level connectivity for GND and VCC.
body:
## Summary

- remove the forced subcircuit behavior from Breakout
- keep Breakout descendants, selectors, traces, and source nets in the enclosing board scope
- let the enclosing board recognize each Breakout as a routing directive and run its fanout configuration as an earlier routing stage
- split cross-boundary traces at breakout points while keeping both sides tied to the original board source trace
- detect cross-boundary traces created below components through connections props

## Why

Breakout describes how a region should be escaped; it should not create selector or net isolation. The previous subcircuit behavior could create a private GND or VCC net inside the Breakout, so escape vias and board-level copper pours had matching names but different connectivity IDs.

With this change, Breakout is an ordinary transparent group. Its routing props configure a bounded fanout stage owned by the enclosing board, and the remaining board connections route afterward around the completed escape copper.

## Regression coverage

- the Breakout source group is not a subcircuit and has no subcircuit ID
- descendants remain selectable from the board
- GND and VCC each resolve to one board source net
- fanout routes plane-terminated GND and VCC escapes to inner pours
- escape vias and target pours share source-net connectivity and the via centers are not cut out of the pours
- cross-boundary traces created by component connections props receive automatic breakout points
- Breakout and subcircuit routing snapshots remain valid

## Checks

- breakout and fanout tests: 11 passed, 2 skipped
- subcircuit and selector regression tests: 59 passed, 2 skipped
- repro79 board-bounds regression: passed

title: Route buses in explicit autorouting phases
description: Changes the autorouting behavior to allow buses to be assigned to explicit routing phases, ensuring that traces within a bus can be routed together in the same phase while preserving their individual phase settings when not explicitly assigned.
body:
## Behavior

Declaring a bus does not select or change a routing phase:

```tsx
<trace
  name="DAT0"
  from=".U1 > .DAT0"
  to=".U2 > .DAT0"
  routingPhaseIndex={0}
/>
<trace
  name="DAT1"
  from=".U1 > .DAT1"
  to=".U2 > .DAT1"
  routingPhaseIndex={1}
/>

<bus name="EMMC_DATA" connections={["DAT0", "DAT1"]} />
```

`DAT0` remains in phase 0 and `DAT1` remains in phase 1. The bus only records their grouping; each phase's autorouter receives the members routed in that phase.

An explicit bus phase assigns every member trace to that phase:

```tsx
<trace name="DAT0" from=".U1 > .DAT0" to=".U2 > .DAT0" />
<trace name="DAT1" from=".U1 > .DAT1" to=".U2 > .DAT1" />

<bus
  name="EMMC_DATA"
  connections={["DAT0", "DAT1"]}
  routingPhaseIndex={1}
/>
```

Both traces are routed with everything else in phase 1.

## Changes

- resolve an explicitly phased bus while core builds its routing-phase plans
- preserve unphased bus membership without changing independently selected trace/net phases
- filter each phase's bus membership to the connections present in that phase
- update to the released `@tscircuit/props@0.0.602` schema from tscircuit/props#769
- add TSX integration coverage for both behaviors

`SimpleRouteJson` is unchanged. Bus objects sent to autorouters still contain only the existing autorouter-facing fields (`busId`, `name`, `connectionNames`, and optional `termination`); they do not contain `routingPhaseIndex`.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/features/autoroutingphase-bus-routing-phase.test.tsx tests/features/autorouter-fanout-plane-termination.test.tsx tests/utils/autorouting/differential-pair-phase-filter.test.ts`

- `bun run smoke-test:dist`
- downstream RK3326 board: 282 PCB traces, 297 vias, zero circuit errors

title: Fix supplier footprint loading without a library resolver
description: Fixes loading of supplier footprints when no library resolver is configured, ensuring components are rendered correctly with pads and ports.
body:
ref #https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/4048
## Summary

- fall back to `partsEngine.fetchPartCircuitJson` when a library footprint has no configured resolver and its prefix/part number matches the component's `supplierPartNumbers`
- preserve configured footprint library resolvers as the preferred loading path
- forward the configured `platformFetch` to the parts engine
- emit `external_footprint_load_error` when no resolver is available or a resolver returns no circuit elements
- add visual regression coverage for supplier fallback and error cases

## Root cause

Library-style footprint strings previously returned early when their platform library resolver was unavailable. This silently produced components without pads, plated holes, or PCB ports.

The fallback is supplier-agnostic: it only uses the parts engine when the footprint reference matches a supplier and part number explicitly declared on the component.

title: Respect routed via layer spans
description: Materializes routed pcb_via.layers from each route points from_layer and to_layer instead of expanding every via across the full board stack, addressing DRC errors caused by treating blind plane drops as through-vias.
body:
## Summary

- materialize routed `pcb_via.layers` from each route point's `from_layer` and `to_layer` instead of expanding every via across the full board stack
- use the same physical span for phased-autorouting via obstacles
- update the existing blind-via, copper-pour, ten-layer, and fanout-plane expectations

## Why

The fanout solver already emits correct plane drops such as `top -> inner1` and `top -> inner2`. Core was preserving those endpoint fields but setting `pcb_via.layers` to every board layer. That made DRC and later routing treat blind plane drops as through-vias, causing false collisions on signal layers beyond the via's physical span.

This surfaced in the RK3326 fanout as 15 USB-to-supply-via DRC errors on `inner3` even though its 205 supply vias terminate on `inner1` or `inner2`.

## Scope

This is intentionally separate from the fanout plane-inference change in #2929. It changes two production call sites and only the existing expectations that encoded full-stack vias.

## Validation

- focused routed-via, copper-pour, ten-layer, and fanout-plane tests: 5 passed, 0 failed
- full CI shard 3: 311 passed, 0 failed
- full CI shard 4: 305 passed, 0 failed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

description: Derives fanout plane drops from an explicit fanoutPourNetMap and infers layer-to-net mapping from copper pour components, allowing users to write source-only traces to GND or VCC and have them drop to the matching pour layer without declaring a singleton BusFanoutTermination.

## Summary

- use source-trace names for optional per-drop fanout directions

## Why

Plane termination belongs to the board's copper intent. Users should be able to
write a normal source-only trace to `net.GND` or `net.VCC` and have fanout drop
it to the matching pour layer without declaring a singleton
`BusFanoutTermination`.

If a net is poured on multiple layers, core reports the ambiguity and asks for

- keep the sequential-trace router's existing two-port limitation unchanged

## Root cause

Both default-router input conversions silently selected only the first two connected ports. A trace such as `[A, B, C]` therefore became `[A, B]`, leaving `C` absent from schematic connectivity and PCB autorouting.

## Fix

The schematic conversion expands an N-terminal trace into adjacent pairwise connections with the same net ID, matching the schematic solver's pair-based input model. The PCB conversion passes all endpoints through `pointsToConnect`, which is the native multi-terminal representation consumed by the capacity autorouter.

## Validation

description: Fixes autorouting failures by normalizing route points and preventing debug image rendering failures from aborting the autorouting process.

## Summary

- document the `--autorouter-debug` stage-image workflow and related SRJ flags
- normalize autorouter `through_obstacle` route points before rendering cumulative stage PNGs

- add regression coverage for both behaviors

Fanout followed by a downstream autorouter can return intermediate
`through_obstacle` route points. Core converts these to Circuit JSON
`through_pad` points before inserting final PCB traces, but the CLI diagnostics
renderer passed the raw points to `circuit-to-svg`. The resulting validation

title: Propagate package licenses into KiCad PCM v2
description: Propagates package licenses from package.json into KiCad PCM v2, ensuring proper license handling and validation in metadata.
body:
## Summary

- propagate `package.json.license` into PCM `packages.json` and archive `metadata.json`
- emit KiCad PCM schema v2 and declare `schema_version: 2` in `repository.json`
- accept schema v2's open license strings while rejecting missing or whitespace-only licenses
- include the declared license when `tsci push` marks a registry release ready to build
- add regression coverage for `CC-BY-ND-4.0`, open-string `Unknown`, missing licenses, and generated v2 metadata

## Root cause

`buildKicadPcm` read the project manifest but did not pass its license to `generatePcmAssets`, whose fallback was `MIT`. The publish path independently omitted the license from `package_releases/update`, leaving the API release at `unset`.

## Impact

Publisher-declared licenses are preserved across PCM artifacts and registry release metadata. PCM output now uses schema v2, whose license field accepts arbitrary strings, and the repository explicitly selects v2 so KiCad validates package metadata with the matching schema. Projects without an explicit license fail with an actionable error instead of being implicitly relicensed.

Schema v2 requires a KiCad version that supports PCM v2 repositories; older KiCad releases that only support v1 cannot consume this feed.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/lib/kicad-pcm-license.test.ts tests/lib/convert-to-kicad-library-with-custom-module.test.ts tests/cli/build/build-kicad-pcm.test.ts tests/cli/build/build-kicad-pcm-paths.test.ts tests/cli/push/push4-create-package.test.ts`

description: Adds a solver-driven snapshot test for detecting BGA cores in mixed-pad packages, addressing detection issues and ensuring proper topology representation.

## What this reproduces

This adds one solver-driven snapshot test for the two topology issues behind `srj24` sample 4:

1. the regular BGA core inside a mixed-pad package is not detected;
2. without BGA-local topology, every package pad stays in the global topology and there is no component-local z0-to-z5 path.

The production code is unchanged in this PR.

## Snapshot

![srj24 sample 4 topology reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/727ed49/tests/features/topology/__snapshots__/srj24-sample4-topology-repro.snap.svg)

The visualization is derived from actual detector, topology-planning, topology-merging, subdivision, and edge-solver output:

- gray: not detected or unassigned to specialized topology;
- blue: owned by global topology;
- red: route terminals;
- the final panel shows that no BGA-local z0-to-z5 path exists.

The exact same test and fixture are used by the stacked fix PR #1799. That PR changes production behavior and naturally updates this same snapshot file.

## Verification

- `bun test tests/features/topology/srj24-sample4-topology-repro.test.ts --timeout 9999999`
- `bun run build`

title: fix(topology): detect BGA cores in mixed packages
description: Fixes detection of BGA cores in mixed packages by isolating the BGA grid from surrounding pads, allowing for proper autorouting connections.
body:
## Stack

Stacked on the test-only reproduction PR #1798.

## Problem

Sample 4 has a regular BGA grid in the middle of a package with different-shaped pads around it. All those pads share the same component ID.

The detector checked every pad together, so the different outer pads prevented it from recognizing the BGA grid.

## Fix

1. Find the regular grid of same-sized, evenly spaced pads inside the package.
2. Treat only that grid as BGA-local. Keep the surrounding pads in the normal global topology.

The existing BGA topology solver can then create the missing connection from the top layer to the bottom layer.

| Reproduction | Fixed |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/727ed49/tests/features/topology/__snapshots__/srj24-sample4-topology-repro.snap.svg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/21104db/tests/features/topology/__snapshots__/srj24-sample4-topology-repro.snap.svg) |

Green pads are the detected BGA core. Blue pads stay global. The last panel shows the BGA-local layer connection.

The fixed path contains more graph nodes, so the SVG table automatically makes its cells wider. The pad coordinates and spacing are unchanged.

## Sample 4 result

Pipeline7 now gets past the original static reachability failure and completes stages 1–10.

It later reaches a separate path-search iteration limit on current `main`. This PR fixes the missing topology, but does not claim that the full sample currently solves.

description: Allows collision-only immutable routes to omit connectivity-map entries during same-net via merging, treating unmapped immutable routes as blocking copper, and retaining hard failure for mutable routes without resolvable nets.
body:
## Summary

- allow collision-only immutable routes to omit connectivity-map entries during same-net via merging
- conservatively treat an unmapped immutable route as different-net blocking copper
- retain the existing hard failure when a mutable route has no resolvable net
- add regression coverage proving the immutable route blocks a via move without being emitted or mutated

## Root cause

Pipeline9 passes pre-routed traces to trace simplification as `otherHdRoutes`. `SameNetViaMergerSolver` includes those routes in its collision index, but it previously required every conflicting route to resolve through the mutable connection map. SRJ23 preloaded fragments have generated IDs such as `source_net_5_fixed_5_2` that are intentionally absent from that map, so simplification failed after routing had already succeeded.

## Impact

This removes the simplification failures for SRJ23 samples 2, 8, and 9 without changing or rerouting the preloaded traces. The targeted benchmark is now 100% solved and 100% relaxed-DRC clean for those three samples.

## Verification

- `bun test tests/features/trace-simplification-immutable-routes.test.ts tests/solvers/same-net-via-merger-direct-overlap-star.test.ts --timeout 60000` (6 passed)

title: Index pin ownership before building chip partitions
description: Reduces the time complexity of building chip partitions by indexing pin ownership, significantly improving performance during the adjacency graph construction.
body:
### Motivation

`ChipPartitionsSolver` previously resolved both endpoints of every strong connection by scanning every chip and its pin list. Building the chip adjacency graph therefore repeated global pin-owner scans and could approach `O(strong connections × chips × pins per chip)` before the connected-component traversal even began.

The same pin-owner map was also reimplemented in several solver paths, and grounded-load layout performed another owner scan after discovery had already found the main chip.

### Evidence

Local synthetic benchmark using a 2,000-chip chain with 3,998 two-way strong-connection entries:

| Revision | Median partition time |
| --- | ---: |
| `b964a93` before index | 327.005 ms |
| `95e3721` with index | 2.479 ms |

Method: Bun 1.3.14, one warm-up followed by seven measured runs on the same machine. This is focused evidence for the removed lookup hotspot, not a universal end-to-end performance claim.

## Summary

The fix adds plated oval hole handling to both board hole-loop generation and 3D hole geometry generation, and also applies \ so rotated oval holes are cut correctly.

## What changed

- add plated \ hole support in \

- fall back to emitted \ / \ when hole-specific dimensions are missing
- apply \ when generating oval plated hole cutouts
- add a unit regression test that verifies the board area is reduced by the expected oval-hole area
- add a snapshot test that reproduces the plated oval hole rendering case end-to-end

## Why this matters

This is a subtle but important core rendering/data-modeling fix:

- it corrects board subtraction for a real plated-hole shape

description: Fixes incorrect rendering for pcb_hole records with hole_shape: oval by adding dedicated ellipse handling for true ellipse rendering instead of rounded slots.
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes incorrect rendering for `pcb_hole` records with `hole_shape: "oval"`.

Previously, `oval` holes were effectively treated like `pill` holes, which produced the wrong board cutout geometry in both loop generation and 3D subtraction. This change adds dedicated ellipse handling so `oval` holes render as true ellipses instead of rounded slots.

## What changed
- Added ellipse loop generation for `oval` PCB holes
- Updated board cutout loop generation to use ellipse geometry for `hole_shape: "oval"`
- Updated 3D hole subtraction to extrude a true ellipse for `oval` holes
- Kept `pill` behavior unchanged
- Added unit coverage for oval-hole subtraction area/wall generation
- Added snapshot coverage for rendered oval-hole output

## Impact
`pcb_hole` objects with `hole_shape: "oval"` and explicit `hole_width`/`hole_height` now render correctly as elliptical board cutouts in both loop-based and 3D board generation paths.

## Root cause
`oval` holes were not given dedicated geometry handling, which caused them to follow the wrong cutout shape path.

## Validation
- `bun test tests/unit/board-geometry.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/snapshot/oval-hole.test.ts`

title: Fix rectangular PCB holes rendering as solid surfaces in 3D
description: Fixes rectangular PCB holes being shown as dark solid surfaces instead of cut-through openings in generated GLTFGLB board models.
body:
## Summary

Fixes rectangular PCB holes being shown as dark solid surfaces instead of cut-through openings in generated GLTF/GLB board models.

## Root cause

Board textures recognized `pcb_hole` elements with `hole_shape: "rect"`, but the 3D geometry pipeline only generated subtraction loops for circular and pill-shaped holes. As a result, the texture displayed an opening while the underlying board mesh remained solid.

## What changed

- Add rectangular loop geometry for `pcb_hole` elements with `hole_shape: "rect"`
- Subtract rectangular holes from the primary triangulated board mesh
- Support rectangular holes in the fallback CSG geometry path
- Generate the four interior walls of rectangular openings
- Replace the deprecated `PCBPlatedHole` test type with `PcbPlatedHole`

## Regression coverage

A regression test reproduces the issue with a 30 mm × 20 mm board containing a 5 mm × 2 mm rectangular hole. It verifies that:

- the rectangular area is removed from the board's top surface
- the opening contains the expected eight interior-wall triangles
- existing circular and plated-hole behavior remains intact

## Verification

- `bun test tests/unit/board-geometry.test.ts`
- `bun test tests/unit/board-geometry.test.ts tests/unit/basic-conversion.test.ts tests/integration/circuit-to-gltf.test.ts`

title: Add a low-memory TypeScript language service toggle
description: Adds a required enableTypeScriptLanguageService prop to CodeEditor and WorkspaceCodeEditor, allowing consumers to keep Monaco editing and syntax highlighting while preventing the TypeScript worker from starting on memory-constrained devices.
body:
## Summary

Adds a required `enableTypeScriptLanguageService` prop to `CodeEditor` and `WorkspaceCodeEditor`, allowing consumers to keep Monaco editing and syntax highlighting while preventing the TypeScript worker from starting on memory-constrained devices.

## Why

Monaco's TypeScript worker loads the compiler and language service into memory. Automatic type acquisition then downloads declaration files into the worker's virtual filesystem, while diagnostics and workspace synchronization retain additional state. Together, these costs can exceed iOS Safari's per-tab or worker memory limit and crash the editor.

The package previously configured these features globally with no consumer-facing way to disable them. This prevented tscircuit.com from safely selecting a lower-memory editor configuration on mobile.

## Changes

- Require consumers to explicitly set `enableTypeScriptLanguageService` on both editor components.
- Disable TypeScript and JavaScript language-service providers when the flag is false, including completion, hover, diagnostics, symbols, references, rename, formatting, code actions, and inlay hints.
- Disable semantic and syntax validation and eager model synchronization.
- Skip automatic type acquisition and workspace worker preparation.
- Skip worker-backed breadcrumb symbol extraction.
- Preserve Monaco editing, syntax highlighting, workspace files, navigation, search, and other non-TypeScript functionality.
- Update examples and README usage to make the decision explicit.

## Consumer usage

```tsx
<WorkspaceCodeEditor
  enableTypeScriptLanguageService={!isMobile}
  {...props}
/>
```

Mobile detection must be available on the initial render so iOS does not briefly initialize the worker before the flag changes.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 57 passed, 0 failed
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`

## Summary

## Algorithm

Columns are sorted by X and nets are indexed in first-seen top-to-bottom order. Every column has an adjacent even and odd gap. A via selects the adjacent gap matching its net parity, receives a per-net track inside that gap, travels vertically to its generated bus row, and finishes at the pad for that net.

- add stable geometry IDs, typed diagnostics, semantic coverage, expected-results manifests, and strict-loss reporting
- add checked binary field readers, a versioned section registry, fixed-layout diagnostics, and safe opaque-section mutation/reserialization
- add public inspection/validation APIs and `inspect`, `validate`, `to-svg`, `to-circuit-json`, and `report` CLI commands
- add an experimental exact-subset Circuit JSON adapter for supported outlines, components, pads, holes, vias, traces, and silkscreen
- make SVG output more Gerber-like with named fabrication layers, reusable apertures, exact drills, stable source-linked elements, compound copper polarity masks, and normalized or source-unit board-coordinate zoom windows
- expand real-board and focused SVG coverage, hostile-input fuzzing, package tests, documentation, security guidance, consolidated CI, and npm provenance publishing

## Verification

- `bun run check`
  - format and TypeScript clean
  - ESM and declarations build successfully
  - **76 passing tests, 2 intentional RK3326 target-file skips, 2,313 assertions**
  - all pinned downloaded ASCII/native fixtures parse and round-trip byte-for-byte

  - `npm pack --dry-run` contains only the intended 8 package files
- GitHub Actions run 3 is green for the package tarball plus the complete Ubuntu and macOS fixture/visual suites

- visually reviewed a 12-view contact sheet covering real ASCII boards, all four native versions in debug mode, front/back copper polarity, drills, and source-unit zoom

## Suggested review order

1. `CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/compatibility.md`, and `docs/public-api.md` for scope/stability
2. `lib/ascii/`, `lib/units.ts`, and geometry normalization/finalization
3. `lib/binary/` and `docs/native-section-map.md`
4. inspection, conversion reports, CLI, and Circuit JSON
5. SVG changes and focused snapshots
6. CI/package/release files

## Deliberately still incomplete

The checklist is intentionally not marked wholesale complete. These items need evidence or inputs that are not safely inventable:

- the authorized RK3326/LPDDR3 target PADS file is not redistributable here, so its two tests remain local/conditional
- undocumented native binary section layouts, references, layer assignments, routes, pad stacks, pours, and connectivity remain partial or opaque; candidates stay out of fabrication layers and only appear in opt-in debug views
- complete PADS ASCII rules/pours/thermals/custom shapes and deterministic fabrication text remain future semantic work
- Circuit JSON conversion is an exact supported subset, not yet full-connectivity or Gerber/Excellon conversion
- independent comparison against PADS or another importer still requires licensed tool access and known-good output

Those limitations are reported through diagnostics/coverage and cause strict conversion to fail instead of silently producing a lossy result.

body:
## What changed

- add a public PCB contour model that preserves source vertices and arc metadata while exposing approximated points, bounds, closure, and winding
- expose board geometry for ASCII and binary documents, including physical board cutouts, layer-stack regions, polygon cutouts, and region holes
- correctly classify the current binary `BoardRegions` corpus as layer-stack regions instead of physical board cutouts
- render physical board cutouts with even-odd SVG fill and render polygon cutouts as substrate before independent copper primitives
- add a board-unit Elk Pi polygon-cutout crop using `bun-match-svg` and `toMatchSvgSnapshot(import.meta.path)`
- centralize verified PCB layer-name normalization and validate primitive layer references against standard, legacy, and document stack-specific names
- update the implementation checklist and public documentation

## Why

The binary fixtures set `ISBOARDCUTOUT=TRUE` on layer-stack regions. Treating that flag literally classified an outline-sized layer-stack region as a physical cutout and would erase the entire board once cutouts were rendered. Separately, the real Elk Pi polygon cutout was painted as translucent green copper instead of exposing the board substrate. Contour decoding also lived only inside the SVG layer, so callers could not inspect the original vertices and arcs semantically.

This PR separates those concepts, retains raw source fields and untouched byte round trips, and makes the distinctions visible in both typed APIs and focused SVG snapshots.

## Summary

This is a broad parser-foundation pass toward the repository checklist. It adds approximately 9,500 lines across syntax preservation, semantic models, validation, editing, project formats, packaging, and tests.

### Parser and AST foundations

- add source locations, stable source-derived node IDs, parent/document links, revisions, dirty tracking, traversal/visitors, cloning, checked transforms, search, structural hashes, and debug JSON
- add strict/compatible/recovery text modes, structured diagnostics, source redaction, cancellation/resource limits, incremental parsing/serialization, and UTF-8/UTF-16/Windows-1252 byte preservation
- add content-based detection and dispatch for PCB/schematic documents, project/workspace/output-job INI files, libraries, ZIP, and XML containers
- add bounded binary readers/writers, preserved enum values, GUID/FILETIME/string codecs, bitfields, and binary payload/source metadata

### PCB and schematic semantics

- expand typed PCB records for boards, components, nets, pads, vias, tracks, arcs, fills, regions, polygons, text, bodies/models, classes, rules, dimensions, rooms, embedded boards, connectivity, and configuration records
- decode binary rule streams and layer-stack metadata
- add revision-aware ownership/reference indexes, dangling-reference reporting, component bounds, PCB connectivity, schematic ownership/hierarchy, and schematic electrical net graphs
- retain all unknown fields, records, streams, and binary payloads for forward-compatible inspection and untouched round trips

### Projects, editing, and serialization

- add source-preserving `PrjPcb`, workspace, OutJob, and generic INI roots with project document graphs, portable Windows-path resolution, variants/settings, output classification, and safe section mutation
- add normalized measurement/geometry inputs and helpers
- add validated copy-on-write PCB transactions, safe net rename, net/layer reassignment, record-level diffs, invertible change sets, and conflict-checked patch application
- define exact/structural/semantic/none round-trip levels, validation-before-write, atomic Node writes, and explicit refusal of unsafe modified binary output

### Tooling, package, and maintenance

- add the `altiumts` CLI (`inspect`, `tree`, `streams`, `records`, `validate`, `roundtrip`, `diff`, `extract`, and `fixture-info`)
- add the `altiumts/node` export, Node 20 metadata, source maps, package self-import verification, a browser smoke bundle, and package/browser size budgets
- add corpus schema inventory and parse/serialize benchmark scripts
- update vulnerable transitive tooling overrides; add CodeQL, Dependabot, security/contributor docs, compatibility/architecture/round-trip docs, and a changelog

## Visual and corpus verification

The refreshed nine-file reference corpus passes without SVG snapshot drift, including full binary PCBs, top/bottom and overlay layers, component/net isolation, slot and rounded-rectangle pads, middle pad stacks, dense routing, and board-unit crops.

The schema audit reports zero unregistered record classes in the current corpus. The checklist now has 565 completed items and 243 deliberately open items. Remaining work is explicitly limited to areas that still need legal fixtures, verified undocumented framing, licensed Altium reopen tests, or substantial follow-on features such as library roots, binary writing, Circuit JSON adapters, fuzzing, and a browser inspector.

## Validation

## What changed

Decoding the verified extended fields lets each layer view use the source pad-stack geometry rather than reusing the top-layer approximation.

- the current binary fixture has 39 extended pad-stack records: 37 round-hole records and 2 slot-hole records

## What changed

- decode binary `WideStrings6` and `Texts6` records, including font and orientation metadata
- decode `ShapeBasedRegions6`, `Regions6`, and `BoardRegions`
- expose authoritative source regions separately from generated region-fill caches
- serialize region contours, holes, text, and curved board/polygon vertices to SVG
- add board-coordinate `viewBox` crops to full-board and per-layer PCB SVG serializers
- cull non-intersecting primitives from focused crops
- render rotated asymmetric round pads as obround/stadium geometry and use rotated bounds for crop selection
- honor parent component `NAMEON`/`COMMENTON` flags unless `showHidden: true` is requested
- add full-board, per-layer, and focused visual snapshots for Elk Pi and SimpleFOC Mini
- update the parser roadmap and current-scope documentation

## Why

The binary PCB renderer previously omitted pour-region geometry and most overlay text, which made complex Altium boards difficult to compare visually. Focused board-coordinate crops make dense features practical to inspect and snapshot. Those close-up views exposed parity problems in pad rotation and component metadata visibility, which are fixed here.

Preserving source regions separately from generated fill caches also prevents cached pour geometry from becoming the semantic source of truth.

## Visual investigation notes

- Elk Pi top-copper and bottom-routing crops now show coherent rotated pads, traces, vias, and pours.
- Close inspection caught asymmetric `ROUND` pads being drawn as mathematical ellipses; they now use true obround/stadium geometry with straight sides and semicircular ends.
- Component designator/comment visibility now follows the source component settings, substantially reducing false overlay clutter.
- The SimpleFOC Mini ASCII `Board` contour is materially larger than its populated/keepout contour; the renderer preserves that source contour for now and the roadmap tracks alternate `POLYGONOUTLINE` contour inference.
- Embedded/custom Altium font decoding remains pending, so some Elk Pi logo glyphs still use system-font fallback shapes.

## Summary

- add a living implementation roadmap for taking `altiumts` from the ASCII `.PcbDoc` prototype to a production-quality parser/editor toolkit
- track 781 concrete items across 29 sections
- distinguish existing prototype capabilities from future work
- cover format research, ASCII and binary PCB files, CFB containers, schematics, libraries, projects, output jobs, semantic references, safe serialization, validation, fuzzing, performance, tooling, tscircuit integration, documentation, releases, and milestone exit criteria

## Design principle

title: Serialize chip pin capabilities to source ports
description: Explicitly maps every PinCapability to its canonical Circuit JSON supports_ source-port field and maps activeCapabilities and activeCapability to corresponding is_configured_for_ fields, ensuring accurate serialization of pin capabilities.
body:
## Summary

- explicitly map every `PinCapability` to its canonical Circuit JSON `supports_*` source-port field
- explicitly map `activeCapabilities` and `activeCapability` to the corresponding `is_configured_for_*` fields
- type the serialization boundary as `SourcePinAttributes` and test all eight supported capabilities

## Why

Core already copied electrical and pull-mode pin attributes to `source_port`, but it dropped capability metadata. As a result, model-specific components could describe RP2040 I2C/SPI/UART mux support in TSX while the generated Circuit JSON lost it.

Each capability now uses an exhaustive switch with a direct, named property assignment. This avoids computed string keys, checks every assignment against `SourcePinAttributes`, and makes additions to the `PinCapability` union a compile-time exhaustiveness error until they are mapped deliberately.

## Scope note

`PinAttributeMap.isGpio` is not included because Circuit JSON does not currently define an `is_gpio` source-port field. Adding that requires a schema change in `tscircuit/circuit-json` before core can serialize it canonically.

## Validation

## Summary

- resolve selectors such as `.ANT1` within the keepout's subcircuit
- serialize the selected components as `excluded_pcb_component_ids` on the `pcb_keepout` Circuit JSON element
- leave Simple Route JSON and every autorouter keepout obstacle unchanged

## Package responsibilities

Core only resolves TSX selectors and emits stable Circuit JSON IDs. It does not inspect or filter DRC output. The actual keepout exemption is implemented in `@tscircuit/checks`.

## Released dependencies

- `circuit-json@^0.0.457`, released from tscircuit/circuit-json#670
- `@tscircuit/checks@0.0.147`, released from tscircuit/checks#176

## Behavior

```tsx
<keepout
  shape="rect"
  width="8mm"
  height="6mm"
  excludeRefs={[".ANT1"]}
/>
```

The resulting keepout contains ANT1's resolved PCB component ID. Autorouters still receive a hard obstacle with an empty `connectedTo` list. Manually routed traces connected to ANT1 do not produce that keepout-overlap error, while unrelated violations remain visible.

## What changed

## Why

The fanout solver needs the physical shape of existing via obstacles to evaluate diagonal clearances correctly. Inferring that shape from an identifier prefix inside the solver is brittle and crosses the serialization boundary. This does not add routing-phase data or automatic bus behavior to Simple Route JSON.

title: Fix schematic text orientation and multipart rendering
description: Fixes schematic text orientation and rendering of multipart components to adhere to Altiums specifications, ensuring proper display of text and symbols in schematic diagrams.

## Summary

- honor Altium's nine text-justification positions and upright left/down orientation rules
- stop combining record orientation with the sheet font table's rotation, which turned the TI vertical net label by 180 degrees
- render only the active unit of multipart schematic symbols
- decode `PinConglomerate` orientation, visibility, name, and designator flags and position pin text on the proper side of the symbol body

## Root cause

The SVG renderer treated font-table rotation as an additional record transform and centered every label vertically. It also rendered every child record of a multipart component, regardless of `CurrentPartId`, and treated pins without an explicit `Orientation` field as right-facing instead of decoding their `PinConglomerate` bitfield. On dense TI sheets this stacked inactive component bodies and hundreds of pins, making the text look oversized and sending net labels and pin text in the wrong direction.

## Summary

- implement the first comprehensive `pads-to-circuit-json` conversion pipeline with stable source-linked IDs, schema validation, mapping coverage, strict/permissive modes, progress reporting, and cancellation
- convert decoded boards, circular and polygonal cutouts, layer stacks, components, ports, nets, routes, vias, copper regions, keepouts, silkscreen, fabrication artwork, component labels, and static footprint text
- preserve compound plated-hole geometry for circular, rectangular, pill, slotted, offset, rounded, and chamfered source pads without emitting duplicate SMT pads
- account explicitly for every skipped or approximated normalized entity, including thermal reliefs and antipads whose source ground-plane ownership is not yet verified

## Why

PADS parsing and Circuit JSON conversion now live in separate packages. This PR establishes the adapter boundary without moving conversion policy back into `padsts`, and makes lossy behavior observable instead of silently dropping unsupported data.

## Dependency

This branch pins merged `padsts/main` commit `a01e301` from tscircuit/padsts#2 for the normalized geometry and source-provenance additions used by the adapter.
