title: Expand canonical symbols and collapse multi-pad MOSFETs
description: Maps Altium MOSFETs to canonical schematic symbols, collapses multi-pad MOSFETs into single schematic ports, and ensures correct representation of various components in Circuit JSON.
body:
## What changed

- map Altium MOSFETs to canonical `schematic-symbols` N/P-channel enhancement/depletion symbols, including 5- and 8-pad power packages
- retain every physical source port and its source-trace membership while collapsing equivalent drain/source pads to one idiomatic schematic port
- prune only the redundant package-pad wire branches, leaving a clean gate/drain/source schematic without losing electrical connectivity
- map two- and four-pin crystals, ferrite beads, and polarized capacitors to their canonical symbols
- emit typed Circuit JSON `simple_mosfet` and `simple_crystal` source components where the Altium pin model is compatible
- match MOSFET ports by functional `gate`/`drain`/`source` aliases before numeric pin labels
- select symbol orientation using all assigned port-pair vectors instead of only the first two ports
- place equivalent four-pin crystal ground pins by side geometry, avoiding crossed schematic leads while preserving their shared net
- route native-symbol lead bridges orthogonally onto the original Altium terminal grid instead of drawing diagonal connections
- parse the primary token of compound component values, fixing cases such as `100uF_50V` being interpreted as `100 F`
- refresh affected SimpleFOC and TI schematic SVG snapshots and add focused semantic/render regressions

## Why

High-resolution comparison of the Altium and Circuit JSON SVGs showed recognizable parts still rendered as generic boxes. Multi-pad power MOSFETs were especially misleading: electrically they are three-terminal devices, but their package pads produced tall generic boxes and redundant wire combs in the schematic.

## Impact

Converted schematics now use substantially more idiomatic Circuit JSON symbols, retain all package-level source connectivity, and join imported wiring with clean orthogonal leads. Crystal frequencies and compound passive values also carry correct numeric semantics downstream.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 68 tests passed, 558 assertions, including all 57 TI schematic sheets and the TI PCB snapshot
- `bunx biome check .`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`
- focused semantic assertions cover three-pin and multi-pad MOSFETs, physical/source vs. schematic port counts, grouped drain connectivity, two/four-pin crystals, ferrite beads, polarized capacitors, compound values, and orthogonal lead edges
- visually inspected high-resolution source/Circuit JSON crops and whole-page comparisons for the affected TI sheets, including the three-MOSFET banks on sheets 32 and 35

title: Connect imported nets to canonical schematic symbol ports
description: Promotes schematic-symbols to a runtime dependency and uses its native symbol metadata during Altium conversion, ensuring standard Circuit JSON symbols retain their canonical geometry while remaining connected to the exact Altium net topology.
body:
## What changed

- promote `schematic-symbols` to a runtime dependency and use its native symbol metadata during Altium conversion
- select directional symbol variants by matching Altium pins to canonical port labels and geometry
- place standard symbols at their native size and map Circuit JSON schematic ports onto their native terminal coordinates
- preserve the original Altium electrical terminal with explicit schematic lead traces between the canonical symbol port and imported net
- add focused TP98 geometry/connectivity assertions and corpus-wide detached-port checks
- reject rendered SVGs containing port-match failures, missing symbols, or invalid coordinates
- refresh the SimpleFOC and affected TI schematic SVG snapshots

## Why

The initial semantic conversion selected standard symbol names but left schematic ports at Altium's original pin spacing. `circuit-to-svg` matches those ports against the canonical `schematic-symbols` geometry, so stretched components—especially one-pin test points—could produce `Could not match ports` and appear visually detached from their traces.

## Impact

Standard Circuit JSON symbols now retain their canonical geometry while remaining connected to the exact Altium net topology. Downstream rendering no longer needs to infer or stretch symbol ports to reach imported wires.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 63 tests passed, including all 57 TI schematic sheets and the TI PCB snapshot
- `bunx biome check .`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`
- all connected standard-symbol ports in the TI and SimpleFOC SVG tests are asserted to have a schematic trace edge
- visually inspected representative TI sheets 14, 17, 24, 33, and 53, including a focused testpoint/lead zoom

title: Convert Altium schematics to idiomatic Circuit JSON
description: Converts Altium components into typed Circuit JSON source components and source ports, emits standard schematic symbols, bridges terminals, and converts electrical connectivity into source nets and traces, enhancing compatibility with Circuit JSON tooling.
body:
## What changed

- convert Altium components into typed Circuit JSON source components and source ports
- emit standard `schematic-symbols` symbols for resistors, capacitors, inductors, diodes, LEDs, test points, power, and ground
- use each standard symbol's native size, center, port labels, and port coordinates when selecting its orientation and placing Circuit JSON schematic ports
- bridge native symbol terminals to the original Altium electrical terminal with explicit schematic trace lead segments
- emit box-with-pins schematic components for chips, connectors, and other multi-pin parts
- convert electrical connectivity into source nets/source traces and schematic traces with explicit port endpoints
- resolve pin terminals and labels anywhere along wire segments, while preserving unconnected crossings
- merge multipart Altium symbols into one physical source component with separate schematic boxes
- refresh the SimpleFOC and all 57 TI TMDS62LEVM schematic snapshots
- add focused semantic, multipart, rendered-symbol, and detached-port regression tests

## Why

The previous converter primarily replayed Altium drawing primitives. That preserved the source styling, but it did not produce idiomatic Circuit JSON that downstream tools can reason about as components, ports, nets, and standard symbols.

The first semantic-symbol implementation selected a symbol name while leaving ports at Altium's original pin-terminal spacing. `circuit-to-svg` matches ports against the native `schematic-symbols` geometry, so stretched symbols—especially one-pin test points—could render with `Could not match ports` and appear detached from their traces.

## Impact

Consumers now receive semantic schematic data suitable for Circuit JSON tooling. Standard symbols render at their canonical geometry, while short lead traces preserve the imported Altium net topology. The converted SVG intentionally uses Circuit JSON's visual language instead of attempting to imitate Altium's symbol styling.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 63 tests passed, including all 57 TI schematic sheets and the TI PCB snapshot
- `bunx biome check .`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`
- `git diff --check`
- every connected standard-symbol port in the TI and SimpleFOC SVG tests is asserted to have a schematic trace edge

description: Preserves native sheet-port direction, height, fill color, and text color in Circuit JSON, emits orientation-aware supply, signal-ground, power-ground, and chassis-ground geometry, fixes pin text scaling, wraps, clips, aligns, and fills Altium text frames, renders imported schematic comparisons without unrelated fixed A4 decoration, and adds focused TI page 17 semantic regression tests.

description: Add a public TypeScript API for converting Altium PCB and schematic documents parsed by altiumts into Circuit JSON, including conversion of PCB outlines, component bounds, copper tracks, vias, and schematic elements, along with validation and caching of fixtures.
body:
## Summary

- add a public TypeScript API for converting Altium PCB and schematic documents parsed by `altiumts` into Circuit JSON
- convert PCB outlines/cutouts, component bounds, copper tracks, vias, detailed pad and hole geometry, and top/bottom silkscreen
- convert schematic sheets, traces, graphics, pins, junctions, ports, labels, text, and active multipart records
- add checksum-pinned open-source fixtures, including the official TI SPRCAL9 / TMDS62LEVM Rev. B design package

- provide `bun run convert:ti-reference` to write the PCB, every schematic sheet, and a manifest as validated Circuit JSON artifacts
- cache the large checksum-verified fixture corpus in CI while keeping source and generated artifacts out of git
- add standard format, typecheck, test, and public npm `bun-pver-release.yml` workflows

## Visual QA findings fixed

- decode numeric Altium `WIDESTRING` text before emitting PCB silkscreen text
- preserve unequal `ROUND` pads as pill geometry instead of collapsing them to circles
- preserve slot, rotated pill, octagonal, rounded-rect, and non-plated pad/hole cases
- constrain PCB comparison viewports to the actual board outline so off-board fabrication/helper primitives do not distort the board regression

## Validation

- `bun run test` (61 tests, 253 assertions; all 57 TI sheets and the TI PCB included)
- `bun run convert:ti-reference` (62,935 PCB elements and 57 independently validated schematic outputs)
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run lint`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build`
- `npm pack --dry-run`

## Follow-up areas

This is the initial conversion layer. The committed comparisons intentionally expose remaining parity gaps, especially embedded schematic images, complete source/connectivity and component semantics, copper pours/regions, mechanical/dimension primitives, models, and project hierarchy.

## What changed

- replace the six hand-authored JSON-only fixtures with six TSX-authored boards that generate routed SRJ
- model realistic USB-C controller, motor driver, LED matrix, Li-ion charger, LED buck driver, and inline power-monitor circuits
- use registry components and real package/part metadata, including datasheet-correct AP2112K, TP4056, PT4115, and ACS37800 footprints and pin mappings
- encode voltage, maximum current, purpose, and nominal trace width for each power rail, resolving every rail to its generated SRJ connection
- add deterministic generation, source-provenance validation, and CI drift detection
- update Cosmos fixtures to describe the real application and rail requirements

## Why

The original corpus started from small synthetic SRJ objects. That did not exercise the intended workflow or resemble boards with real power-distribution constraints. The dataset needs to represent the late pipeline handoff from ordinary autorouting to power-trace widening while remaining reproducible from tscircuit source.

## Impact

Consumers now receive fully routed SRJ generated from inspectable `.circuit.tsx` sources. Base copper is normalized to 0.15 mm while authored `nominalTraceWidth` requirements are preserved, so `power-trace-solver` has realistic connected boards to expand.

title: Fix via connectsTo connectivity
description: Fixes connectivity issues by ensuring that vias correctly associate with both component ports and nets, allowing for proper autorouting and short detection.
body:
## Summary

- resolve `via.connectsTo` port and net selectors into an ordinary source trace
- associate the manual source via and physical PCB via with that connectivity
- emit the semantic `pcb_via.source_trace_id` without overloading `pcb_trace_id` with a source ID
- omit `source_manually_placed_via.source_net_id` until a real net is assigned
- keep the implementation local to `Via`; the earlier `Group` refactor and extra lifecycle hook have been removed

## Root cause

`Via` previously only inspected `net.*` selectors when assigning PCB connectivity. It ignored port selectors, did not create referenced nets, and serialized a blank `source_net_id`. As a result, the component pad and via were separate logical owners even when `connectsTo` explicitly joined them.

The via now creates a normal `source_trace` for its selected ports and nets, then references that trace from the source and PCB via records. Net-only vias retain their existing `pcb_trace_id` fallback until Circuit JSON has a dedicated PCB-via net reference.

## Dependencies and merge order

1. tscircuit/circuit-json#672 added `pcb_via.source_trace_id`.
2. tscircuit/circuit-json#674 made unassigned manual-via source net IDs optional and non-empty; both schema changes are consumed through `circuit-json@0.0.459`.
3. tscircuit/circuit-json-to-connectivity-map#34 consumes the new source-trace relationship; this PR uses the released `circuit-json-to-connectivity-map@0.0.26`.
4. tscircuit/check-shorts#31 upgrades the short detector to that connectivity-map release and adds a false-positive regression. Merge and release it before this PR.

## Impact

Via-in-pad connections now satisfy source pin/netlist checks, participate in autorouter obstacle connectivity, and are recognized as same-net geometry by short detection.

Part of tscircuit/tscircuit#4205. Validated against the four GND vias in tscircuit/nrf52810#1.

## Validation

- regression test for a via connecting a component port to `net.GND`
- regression test proving a port-only via omits `source_net_id` instead of writing an empty string
- footprint via obstacle-connectivity regression
- footprint thermal-via connectivity regression
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Preserve schematic rail placement and expose solver inputs
description: Preserves schematic rail placement by honoring power and ground attributes when replacing net labels with rail symbols, and exposes solver constructor arguments for better traceability.
body:
## Summary

- honor `source_net.is_power` and `source_net.is_ground` when replacing schematic net labels with rail symbols, including names such as `USB_5V` and `LOGIC_3V3`
- preserve the schematic trace solver's selected net-label orientation when core recenters a nearby GND label
- add `solverConstructorArgs` to every current core `solver:started` emitter while retaining the existing `solverParams` field
- add visual regressions for explicit power nets and the exact XIAO RP2040 + A4988 pin geometry

## Root cause

The schematic trace solver correctly rejected a downward GND symbol beside the XIAO's tightly spaced `3V3` and `D10` pins and selected a horizontal label. Core's later missing-trace label pass overwrote that `anchor_side` with `top`, which turned it into an intersecting `rail_down` symbol.

The rail-symbol replacement pass also inferred power only from a name regex. It ignored the explicit `source_net.is_power` / `is_ground` attributes, so names with a non-voltage prefix did not receive the requested symbol.

`tsci check schematic-placement` did not report this because it validates schematic component boxes and pin spacing; the collision was introduced later by net-label postprocessing.

## Validation

- final focused event/rail/orientation suite: 11 passed, 0 failed

title: Add photodiode spectral selectivity filters
description: Adds functionality to rank photodiodes by distance from their peak wavelength, allowing users to exclude certain peak bands and keep the target near a devices peak response.
body:
## Summary

- rank target-wavelength matches by distance from their peak wavelength, then by stock
- add `peak_distance_max` to keep the target near a device's peak response
- add `excluded_peak_bands` for comma-separated peak wavelengths or ranges such as `700-1100, 532`
- add field guidance and explain that catalog metadata is not a full spectral-responsivity curve

Example for a 355 nm search that rejects IR-peaking devices:

```text
/photo_diodes/list?wavelength=355&peak_distance_max=100&excluded_peak_bands=700-1100
```

## Why

The catalog only exposes peak wavelength and advertised spectral-range endpoints. A range containing 355 nm does not mean the device responds strongly there, which caused 820–950 nm-peaking parts to dominate the results. Peak proximity is the most defensible available proxy for target sensitivity, while excluded peak bands let users remove parts optimized for unwanted regions without pretending the catalog contains full responsivity curves.

This builds on #433, which renamed the canonical target parameter to `wavelength`.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 181 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit --project cf-proxy/tsconfig.json`
- `bun run format:check`

## Summary

- use `wavelength` as the canonical **Target Wavelength** query parameter while preserving `wavelength_min` as a legacy alias
- match target wavelengths against the advertised spectral range
- rank matching parts by distance from their peak wavelength, then by stock
- add `peak_distance_max` to keep the target near a device's peak response
- add `excluded_peak_bands` for comma-separated peak wavelengths or ranges such as `700-1100, 532`
- explain in the UI that catalog metadata is not a full spectral-responsivity curve and that optical filtering may still be required

Example for a 355 nm search that rejects IR-peaking devices:

```text
/photo_diodes/list?wavelength=355&peak_distance_max=100&excluded_peak_bands=700-1100
```

## Why

The catalog only exposes peak wavelength and advertised spectral-range endpoints. A range containing 355 nm does not mean the device responds strongly there, which caused 820–950 nm-peaking parts to dominate the results. Peak proximity is the most defensible available proxy for target sensitivity, while excluded peak bands let users remove parts optimized for unwanted regions without pretending the catalog contains full responsivity curves.

## Validation

title: Filter Photo Diodes by detection range
description: Changes the filtering mechanism for photo diodes to match detection ranges based on a desired wavelength instead of just peak wavelength, improving accuracy in results.
body:
## Summary

- make the existing `wavelength_min` parameter represent a desired wavelength
- match photodiodes whose published spectral range contains that wavelength
- fall back to an exact peak-wavelength match only when a part has no complete spectral range
- relabel the UI field from **Min Wavelength** to **Desired Wavelength**

## Root cause

The previous filter compared the requested value only to `peak_wavelength_nm` using `>=`. A request for 300 nm therefore returned IR-only parts with 940 nm peaks and 840–1100 nm detection ranges.

The new predicate is:

```text
spectral_range_min_nm <= desired_wavelength <= spectral_range_max_nm
```

For incomplete range data, `peak_wavelength_nm = desired_wavelength` is used as a conservative fallback.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 181 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit --project cf-proxy/tsconfig.json`
- `bun run format:check`
- integration coverage verifies that 840–1100 nm is excluded for 300 nm, while 300–1100 nm is included

title: Repair DRC conflicts with safe trace layer moves
description: Fixes DRC conflicts by implementing safe trace-layer repairs that prevent routing regressions and ensure full-board DRC improvements without increasing via-related DRC errors.
body:
## Issue

Pipeline 7 can finish with trace-to-trace or pad-to-trace DRC errors. Moving an entire route to another layer fixed some of these errors, but routes connected to terminals received layer transitions inside their pads. That introduced via-in-pad geometry and caused routing regressions. Incomplete repairs could also be kept even when trace DRC remained.

## Implementation

This PR enables the safe trace-layer repair implemented in [high-density-repair03#41](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/41).

The repair:

- selects the same-layer span nearest the DRC conflict instead of moving the whole route
- tries deterministic, bounded span expansions on another legal layer
- reuses existing layer transitions for internal spans
- places terminal transitions beyond the connected pad boundary
- accepts a candidate only when full-board DRC strictly improves without increasing via-related DRC
- commits the repair phase only when all trace and pad-to-trace errors are resolved; otherwise it restores the original routes

This is one repair operation with separate handling for internal and terminal boundaries. Existing via-in-pad behavior remains opt-in.

## Validation

The before/after SVG test covers both boundary cases and verifies DRC improves from 2 errors to 0 while terminal identities are preserved. All hosted build, format, typecheck, and test checks pass.

title: Repair trace conflicts with transactional layer moves
description: Adds a safe trace-layer repair operation to resolve trace conflicts by moving routes to another layer while ensuring DRC compliance and rollback capabilities.
body:
## Issue

The DRC repair solver could resolve trace conflicts by moving an entire route to another layer. For terminal routes, this placed new layer transitions at pad centers and introduced via-in-pad geometry. It could also retain a partial repair while trace or pad-to-trace DRC errors remained.

## Implementation

This PR adds one safe trace-layer repair operation to `GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver`:

- find the same-layer route span nearest the reported conflict
- try deterministic, bounded expansions of that span on another legal layer
- reuse adjacent layer transitions and remove obsolete hops for internal spans
- extend terminal-reaching spans beyond the connected pad before changing layers
- score each materialized candidate against full-board DRC
- accept only strict DRC improvements that do not increase via-related errors

The operation runs as a transactional phase. It commits only after all trace-to-trace and pad-to-trace errors are resolved; otherwise the original route set is restored. Unrelated DRC classes remain available to downstream repair stages.

## Validation

Focused tests cover internal transition reuse, terminal transitions outside pads, rollback of incomplete repairs, and successful commits when only unrelated DRC classes remain. The dependent [autorouter PR #1810](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/1810) contains the hosted before/after SVG. Formatcheck, typecheck, and tests pass.

title: Migrate footprint IoU scoring to Manifold 2D boolean geometry
description: Migrates footprint IoU scoring from rasterized geometry to deterministic Manifold 2D boolean geometry, ensuring consistent scoring across different resolutions and improving performance.
body:
# Migrate footprint IoU scoring to Manifold 2D boolean geometry

## Motivation

Footprint comparison previously rasterized copper and hole geometry onto a pixel grid. This caused scores to vary depending on whether discovery used a `112×112` grid or final validation used a `320×320` grid.

Rasterization could also hide small dimensional differences or select a different best candidate at another resolution.

## Implementation

- Added `@tscircuit/manifold-2d` as a direct dependency.
- Converted pads and holes into deterministic Manifold polygons.
- Added support for:
  - Rectangles and rounded rectangles
  - Pills
  - Circles and ellipses
  - Polygon pads
  - Arbitrary rotations
- Unioned overlapping shapes before measuring their area.
- Calculated IoU using Manifold intersection and union areas.
- Used the same comparison method for discovery and final validation.
- Preserved raster occupancy exclusively for the Fast Footprint Compare heatmap.
- Updated precision-sensitive tests that previously relied on raster rounding.
- Updated the AP2112 regression to expect its semantically correct `sot25` match.
- Updated benchmark documentation to describe Manifold-based scoring.

## Validation

- `bun test`: **103 passed, 0 failed**
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: passed
- `bun run format:check`: passed
- `bun run build`: passed
- Fast Footprint Compare tests and typecheck: passed
- Fast Footprint Compare production build: passed
- Browser Manifold WASM initialization: passed with no runtime errors

### Controlled 50-part benchmark

- Before: 43/50 at or above 95% IoU
- After: 43/50 at or above 95% IoU
- Before duration: 54.1 seconds
- After duration: 10.5 seconds
- Speed improvement: approximately **5.15×**

### Full JLC5000 benchmark

- **484/600** parts at or above 95% IoU
- 116 parts below the threshold
- 0 errors
- 121 seconds total
- No previously passing part fell below the 95% threshold

title: Remove sample001 redundant via pair
description: Removes unnecessary via pairs from the autorouting process when endpoints are blocked by pad-clearance envelopes, ensuring a cleaner routing path without additional vias.
body:
## What changed

- lets via-pair cleanup consider one immediately adjacent same-layer anchor when a landing endpoint is blocked by a pad-clearance envelope
- preserves the original cleanup interval as the first candidate
- restricts expansion to pairs that already have a quality-valid base candidate and endpoints blocked specifically by pads
- updates the sample001 end-to-end assertion from the reproduced pair to zero final vias
- adds a focused post-cleanup SVG snapshot using the same layer-based autorouter rendering as the reproduction

## Root cause

The expander legitimately chose a temporary bottom-layer detour. Cleanup then tried to replace only the interval between the immediate via landing wires. Those endpoints intersected the clearance envelope of Pico pad `pcb_smtpad_37`, so the grid fallback rejected the route before searching. The neighboring top-layer anchors were clear but outside the cleanup interval.

## Visual result

The pre-cleanup snapshot in #7 remains unchanged and shows the red/blue layer excursion with two vias. This PR adds `sample001-via-pair-after-cleanup.snap.svg`, which shows zero via circles, zero bottom-layer copper, and a top-layer route around the pad.

## Impact

The pair remains observable at the pre-cleanup boundary in the reproduction from #7, proving where it originated. After cleanup, trace `source_net_3_mst10_0` remains entirely on the top layer around the pad with zero vias.

This PR is stacked on #7. After #7 merges, this PR can be retargeted to `main`.

## Validation

- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run typecheck`

title: Rename insertion_direction front/back to top/bottom and add axis aliases
description: Renames insertion_direction Y-axis values from from_frontfrom_back to from_topfrom_bottom and adds from_below for -Z, ensuring all names align with the 2D PCB view.
body:
insertion_direction named its +/-Y values "from_front"/"from_back" while "from_left"/"from_right" already followed the 2D PCB view. This renames the Y-axis values to "from_top" (+Y) and "from_bottom" (-Y) so every name is read off the board as drawn, and adds the missing "from_below" (-Z) to pair with "from_above" (+Z).

"above"/"below" are used for Z rather than "top"/"bottom" so the Z values never collide with the Y ones.

Each direction also gains an equivalent Cartesian spelling ("from_y+", "from_x-", ...). Both spellings are accepted on input and parsing normalizes the Cartesian ones to the named values, so a parsed insertion_direction is always one of the six named values and consumers only handle one spelling.

The field previously had no .describe(); it is now documented, along with a note that these names are unrelated to the layer field's "top"/"bottom".

title: Follow insertion_direction rename to top/bottom
description: Renames the insertion directions in Circuit JSON from from_frontfrom_back to from_topfrom_bottom and adds from_below (-Z), ensuring alignment with the schema and fixing direction mirroring.
body:
Circuit JSON renamed the +/-Y insertion directions from "from_front"/"from_back" to "from_top"/"from_bottom" and added "from_below" (-Z).

The local PcbInsertionDirection union is replaced with Circuit JSON's exported InsertionDirection so this transform cannot silently drift from the schema again; previously it could have written a value the schema no longer accepts.

Mirrored transforms now also flip the Z-axis directions. "from_above" was returned unchanged for any transform, which had no better answer available while "from_below" did not exist.

title: Rename insertionDirection front/back to top/bottom and add axis aliases
description: Renames insertion direction values from from_frontfrom_back to from_topfrom_bottom and adds Cartesian equivalents for better alignment with PCB design.
body:
Follows the matching Circuit JSON change. The +/-Y values are renamed from "from_front"/"from_back" to "from_top"/"from_bottom" so every name is read off the footprint as drawn in the 2D PCB view, "from_below" (-Z) is added to pair with "from_above" (+Z), and each direction gains an equivalent Cartesian spelling ("from_y+", "from_x-", ...).

title: Restore hyphenated SOT-23 aliases
description: Restores support for standard sot-23 footprint strings and normalizes sot-23, sot-23-3, sot-23-5, and sot-23-6 to their canonical SOT-23 definitions, while adding circuit JSON equality checks and PCB SVG snapshots for each alias.
body:
## Summary

- Restore support for standard `sot-23` footprint strings.
- Normalize `sot-23`, `sot-23-3`, `sot-23-5`, and `sot-23-6` to their canonical SOT-23 definitions.

The RJ45 footprint parser change allowed `-` to begin a parameter value so signed values such as `holey-3.43mm` work. Before normalization, that caused `sot-23` to be parsed as `sot("-23")`; the generic six-pin SOT parser then failed validation instead of selecting the standard SOT-23 footprint.

This keeps signed parameter parsing intact while handling the hyphenated SOT-23 family as aliases before tokenization.

title: Pack PCB components independently by layer
description: Partitions PCB packing jobs by layer to optimize component placement and reduce distance between connected components.
body:
Depends on #2989.

## Summary

- partition a `pcbPack` job by resolved PCB component layer before invoking `calculate-packing`
- run the normal sequential optimal solver once per layer, top first
- preserve cross-layer network attraction by carrying already-packed opposite-side pads into later jobs as point-sized collision references
- turn the BGA/bottom-decoupling regression back into a normal passing test and refresh its ratsnest SVG
- refresh the two existing multi-layer packing snapshots whose bottom-side placements correctly change

## Why

`calculate-packing` currently has no layer field in `PackInput`, so one combined solve treats the top-side BGA courtyard as an obstruction for bottom-side capacitors. The reproduction in #2989 measures 16.845747 mm of total straight-line distance across four decoupling connections.

With this change, the same test measures 1.166190 mm (under its 2 mm bound), while same-layer components still use the existing collision geometry and sequential optimal placement algorithm.

## Test plan

- `bun test tests/repros/repro-bottom-layer-bga-decoupling-packing.test.tsx tests/features/pcb-pack-layout tests/features/component-constraints/component-constraints01.test.tsx` (14 pass)
- `bun test tests/repros/repro58-pcb-autolayout-out-of-board.test.tsx tests/examples/example29-copper-pour.test.tsx` (10 pass)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bunx biome check` on changed TypeScript files
- `git diff --check`
- GitHub Actions: all four Bun test shards, typecheck, format-check, smoke-test, and Vercel pass

title: Repro bottom-layer BGA decoupling packing
description: Reproduces a test case where bottom-layer decoupling capacitors are incorrectly placed underneath a BGA due to PCB layer identity not being preserved in packing calculations.
body:
## Summary

- add a minimal 6x6 BGA with two 0402 decoupling capacitors on `layer="bottom"`
- capture the current PCB placement in a visual snapshot
- measure the total Euclidean distance across the four intended BGA-to-capacitor pad connections

## Reproduction

`pcbPack` uses the default `minimum_sum_squared_distance_to_network` placement strategy. A valid bottom-side placement can center C1 and C2 on the two connected BGA rows for about 0.44 mm of total straight-line connection distance.

The current result places the capacitors above and below U1 and measures 16.845747 mm, so the test intentionally fails its generous `< 2 mm` bound.

## Suspected cause

The Circuit JSON conversion into `calculate-packing` does not preserve PCB layer identity in `PackInput`. The packer therefore treats top-side BGA pads as collision geometry for bottom-side components instead of allowing the capacitors to occupy the same XY area on the opposite copper side.

This PR is a test-only failing reproduction; it does not include a fix.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit` — passes
- `git diff --check` — passes
- `bun test tests/repros/repro-bottom-layer-bga-decoupling-packing.test.tsx` — intentionally fails: expected total distance < 2 mm, received 16.84574723780456 mm

title: Fix PCB component rotations inside rotated groups

title: feat: make smtpad solder paste aperture configurable via solderPasteMargin
description: Adds a solderPasteMargin prop to smtpad for configuring the solder paste aperture size, addressing issues with default scaling that resulted in apertures below IPC standards.
body: Fixes #2896 ## What Adds a **`solderPasteMargin`** prop to ``: an absolute per-side margin for the solder paste aperture, mirroring the existing `solderMaskMargin` sign convention (positive grows the aperture, negative shrinks it). A margin of `0` gives a 1:1 aperture. If the margin shrinks an aperture to zero, no `pcb_solder_paste` element is emitted. Today's `0.7 ×` behaviour stays the default when the prop is not set, so nothing changes for existing designs. Uses the prop added in tscircuit/props#767. ## Why `SmtPad.doInitialPcbPrimitiveRender()` shrank every paste aperture to `0.7 ×` the pad dimensions (0.49 of the pad area) with no override. As measured in #2896, on a production panel that put 27% of apertures below the IPC-7525 area-ratio release floor of 0.66 (TAD5242 VQFN: AR 0.500, OPA2210 WSON: AR 0.605) — while the manufacturers' own stencil drawings for those packages specify 1:1 apertures. ## Tests `tests/components/primitive-components/smtpad-solder-paste-config.test.tsx` (8 tests): - default stays `0.7` with no props set (rect + circle) - negative, zero and positive margins on rect (inset, 1:1, overprint) - circle radius gets the margin once per side; width/height twice - rotated_rect honors the margin and keeps its rotation - zero-size aperture ⇒ no `pcb_solder_paste` element emitted - visual snapshots (PCB view + solder paste mask) of the four regimes side by side ## Visual snapshot Four identical 2×1.4mm rect pads, left to right: **no prop (default 0.7×)** · **`solderPasteMargin={0}`** (1:1) · **`solderPasteMargin={-0.2}`** (inset) · **`solderPasteMargin={0.2}`** (overprint): | PCB view | Solder paste mask | | :---: | :---: | | | | The first aperture is the current default; the mask only changes when the prop is set. Full suite: no regressions vs `main` (the only failures on my machine are the same pre-existing `renderUntilSettled` timeout flakes that fail identically on unmodified `main`).

title: Recommend idiomatic identifiers for invalid pin labels
description: Recommends idiomatic identifiers for common voltage pin labels such as 3.3V, 3V3, and 5V, and includes these recommendations in warnings and errors related to pin labels.
body:
## Summary

- recommend idiomatic `V3_3`, `V5`, and related identifiers for common voltage pin labels such as `3.3V`, `+3V3`, and `+5V`
- include the recommendation in both ignored-property warnings and schematic pin-label parse errors
- add regression coverage for chip pin labels and schematic arrangements

## Why

tscircuit pin identifiers only support letters, numbers, and underscores. Common module labels containing `+` or `.` were filtered out, and schematic arrangements could then fail with an opaque error. This can produce empty/black footprint renders when the component never finishes creating.

The new guidance maps common voltage forms to exact idiomatic identifiers, for example:

- `3.3V` or `+3V3` -> `V3_3`
- `+5V` -> `V5`

The actual voltage metadata remains unchanged; only the pin identifier recommendation is normalized.

## Verification

- `bun test tests/components/normal-components/chip-invalid-pin.test.tsx`
- `bun run build`
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`

## Summary

- assign net-only manual PCB vias with source_net_id
- reserve pcb_trace_id for references to actual physical PCB traces
- retain source_trace_id for port-bearing logical trace connectivity
- avoid writing absent connectivity fields as undefined properties

## Connectivity semantics

- pcb_trace_id references a pcb_trace
- source_trace_id references a source_trace
- source_net_id references a source_net

Depends on merged tscircuit/circuit-json#676 and tscircuit/circuit-json-to-connectivity-map#35.

- Biome check passes
- git diff --check

title: Use one resolved boundary for breakout fanout
description: Resolves fanout bounds for each fanout phase by establishing a single boundary based on explicit geometry or padding, ensuring consistent routing and eliminating conflicts between breakout points and fanout boundaries.
body:
## Summary

- resolve one `fanoutBounds` value for each fanout phase
- let explicit breakout geometry establish the bounds, or derive them from `fanoutBoundaryPadding` when no explicit geometry exists
- expand the resolved bounds to include any breakout points
- pass only the resolved `fanoutBounds` into the fanout solver
- synchronize solver-selected fanout exits with the automatic breakout points consumed by the parent/global route
- emit a Circuit JSON warning only when explicit geometry and `fanoutBoundaryPadding` resolve to different bounds

## Boundary resolution

1. Explicit breakout geometry (`width`, `height`, or `outline`) establishes the initial `fanoutBounds`.
2. Without explicit geometry, `fanoutBoundaryPadding` derives `fanoutBounds` from the connected source-pad obstacles.
3. Without either input, the inferred breakout group bounds are used.
4. Breakout points expand the resulting `fanoutBounds` when necessary.

There is no separate fanout boundary or breakout-padding boundary in the routing phase plan. Generic breakout `padding` is not treated as a competing fanout-boundary input.

## Root cause

Automatic breakout points were placed on the `pcb_group` boundary, while the fanout solver independently derived another shared boundary from source pads plus `fanoutBoundaryPadding`. The fanout trace therefore ended at one point and global routing started at another. A capacity-autorouter follow-up had been masking that discontinuity by routing a short boundary continuation.

The fix resolves `fanoutBounds` before fanout starts and uses that single value for the solver and breakout group. After fanout, each solver exit structurally replaces the matching automatic breakout point and global connection endpoint using the routing group and source trace identity. No connection-name or component-ID string heuristic is used.

## Impact

Each chip fanout completes locally at its resolved bounds, then all fanout endpoints are handed to one parent/global routing phase. Standalone fanout phases and genuine internal breakout routing retain their normal default follow-up behavior.

## Validation

- focused breakout/fanout suite: 17 passed, 2 skipped, 0 failed
- breakout-point expansion unit regression
- two-BGA regression proves independent fanouts followed by one global bus route, with all eight endpoints continuous
- RK3326 integration: four independent fanout phases (224, 11, 4, and 10 connections) followed by one 25-connection global phase; zero routing errors
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Follow insertion_direction rename to top/bottom

body: Circuit JSON renamed the +/-Y insertion directions from "from_front"/"from_back" to "from_top"/"from_bottom" and added "from_below" (-Z). Update the mapping to match, treating "from_below" like "from_above": neither constrains an in-plane facing direction, so both yield null.

title: Migrate web editor to Monaco WorkspaceCodeEditor with mobile memory toggle
description: Replaces the CodeMirror-based CodeEditor in CodeAndPreview with WorkspaceCodeEditor from tscircuitmonaco-code-editor (v0.0.22), bringing the workspace UI (file sidebar, breadcrumb symbol navigation, quick-open, cross-file search) to the web editor and implements a mobile memory toggle to prevent out-of-memory issues in mobile Safari.
body:
## What changed

Replaces the CodeMirror-based `CodeEditor` in `CodeAndPreview` with `WorkspaceCodeEditor` from `@tscircuit/monaco-code-editor` (v0.0.22), bringing the workspace UI (file sidebar, breadcrumb symbol navigation, quick-open, cross-file search) to the web editor.

## Mobile memory fix

Monaco's TypeScript worker loads the full compiler plus automatically-acquired `@types`, which OOMs mobile Safari (hard per-tab memory cap). The editor package exposes `enableTypeScriptLanguageService`; this PR gates it so the worker and type acquisition never start on mobile.

The gate uses a dedicated hook (`useEnableMonacoLanguageService`) that **starts `false`** and only flips to `true` once a `min-width: 768px` viewport is confirmed. A conventional `!useIsMobile()`-style check reports `false` (desktop) on the first render, so it would briefly enable the language service and spin the worker up before the effect could correct it — defeating the fix on real devices.

## Changes

- Add `@tscircuit/monaco-code-editor` pinned to `v0.0.22` (git `#9d88fd2`)
- `src/lib/monaco-workers.ts`: register Monaco's editor/ts web workers for Vite (`?worker`) — required or language features silently no-op
- Import the package's precompiled stylesheet in `main.tsx`
- Bump `tsconfig` `lib` to ES2021 (package ships raw TS source using `replaceAll`; `target` unchanged)
- Wire file create/rename/delete and content changes to the existing package-file mutations

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` passes
- Dev server builds cleanly; editor mounts and, on desktop, the TS worker + type acquisition load (full IntelliSense preserved)

### Not verified
Mobile behavior was confirmed at the source level (v0.0.22 disables `modeConfiguration`, `eagerModelSync`, diagnostics, and ATA when the toggle is off) but **not** on a real <768px device — a desktop narrow viewport can confirm TS is disabled but cannot confirm the iOS OOM is resolved. Testing on an actual iOS device is recommended before merge.

title: Fix Ctrl/Cmd+Enter execution when Monaco consumes the shortcut
description: Fixes a keyboard shortcut bug that prevented RunFrame from executing code with CtrlEnter or CmdEnter while Monaco had focus.
body:
## Summary

Fixes a keyboard shortcut bug that prevented RunFrame from executing code with Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter while Monaco had focus.

## Reproduction

1. Open RunFrame with the Monaco editor.
2. Focus the editor.
3. Press Ctrl+Enter on Windows/Linux or Cmd+Enter on macOS.
4. RunFrame does not execute because Monaco consumes the keyboard event before it reaches the existing listener.

## Fix

- Listen for the shortcut during the capture phase so RunFrame receives it before Monaco.
- Prevent Monaco's default behavior when the shortcut is triggered.
- Stop further propagation to avoid duplicate or conflicting actions.
- Preserve the existing guard that prevents another execution while code is already running.

## User impact

Users can now reliably run code with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter without leaving the editor, restoring the advertised shortcut and improving the core editing workflow.

## Testing

Manually verified by applying the change as a patch on tscircuit.com.

Confirmed that Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs code while Monaco is focused and does not trigger Monaco's default behavior.

`bun run build:lib` successfully builds the JavaScript bundles, but declaration generation is currently blocked by an unrelated existing `hideSchematic` type error in `CircuitJsonPreview.tsx`.

title: Prevent power trace expansion from adding vias
description: Default power trace expansion to disallow new vias, ensuring that the output never has more vias than the routed input, while maintaining planar expansion.
body:
## Summary

- default Pipeline7 power expansion to `allowNewVias: false`
- pin the prerequisite power-trace-expander change from tscircuit/power-trace-expander#12
- assert the SRJ27 post-expansion output never has more vias than the routed input
- refresh all six SRJ27 visual snapshots on macOS and Linux

## Root cause

The power trace expander's layer-aware rerouting can insert via pairs while widening a necked route. On SRJ27 this increased via counts substantially (for example, sample003 went from 14 to 26 and sample004 from 2 to 11).

No-new-vias mode skips layer-changing candidates while retaining planar/in-place expansion. Pipeline7 enables that mode by default, while still allowing an explicit override through `powerTraceExpansion.allowNewVias`.

The recent core QFP/SOIC snapshot changes were investigated separately. The expander inserted zero vias in those cases; their added vias come from safe DRC layer repair introduced in v0.0.733 and fix real pad overlap/clearance errors. This PR intentionally keeps those repairs.

## SRJ27 results

| Sample | Before (pre→post vias) | After (pre→post vias) | DRC (pre→post) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 001 | 5→9 | 5→5 | 1→0 |
| 002 | 5→11 | 5→5 | 1→1 |
| 003 | 14→26 | 14→14 | 1→0 |
| 004 | 2→11 | 2→2 | 2→0 |
| 005 | 4→4 | 4→4 | 0→0 |
| 006 | 14→16 | 14→14 | 2→2 |

The DRC-clean set remains 001, 003, 004, and 005. Solve completion remains 6/6.

## /benchmark-all

| Dataset | Main completed | PR completed | Main DRC | PR DRC |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dataset01 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 88.2% | 88.2% |
| SRJ18 | 62.5% | 68.8% | 12.5% | 12.5% |
| SRJ19 | 87.5% | 88.0% | 34.0% | 34.0% |
| SRJ20 | 71.5% | 73.0% | 27.5% | 27.5% |
| SRJ21 | 100.0% | 100.0% | 90.0% | 90.0% |
| SRJ23 | 97.4% | 97.4% | 19.7% | 19.7% |

No benchmark dataset regressed in relaxed DRC pass rate. Completion was unchanged or improved.

## Validation

- `bun test tests/pipeline7-post-processing-before-power-expansion.test.ts tests/features/pipeline7-power-trace-expansion-visual.test.ts`
- `bun test --timeout 9999999`: 440 pass, 55 skip, 0 fail
- focused Linux CI shard 4 snapshot update and verification passed

title: Preserve same-net rail alignment without touching other nets
description: Preserves same-net rail alignment without allowing rendered strokes to touch parallel traces from another net, ensuring valid perpendicular crossings and point contacts while introducing a fallback for alignment when necessary.
body: ## Summary - preserve same-net rail alignment without allowing rendered strokes to touch parallel traces from another net - evaluate the existing rail coordinates first, preserving the previous layout whenever one is valid - only when every original coordinate is blocked by a touching parallel trace, derive a fallback with a visible cross-net gap - keep perpendicular crossings and point contacts valid - add a generic cleanup-solver regression and a BQ25895 integration assertion ## Root cause `TraceOverlapShiftSolver` correctly separated the original coincident traces. A later `TraceCleanupSolver2` pass aligned two GND rails for readability at `x = -3.35`, while CE was at `x = -3.33`. The centerlines were one rendered trace width (`0.02`) apart, so their strokes touched. The cleanup alignment stage originally checked exact centerline coincidence, not rendered stroke overlap. The first correction rejected the touching coordinate, but left the two GND pieces unaligned. A subsequent version generated candidates using the solver's obstacle `paddingBuffer`; that was the wrong policy and let unrelated clearance coordinates compete with already-valid alignments, moving repro130 and example02. The final algorithm is a strict two-pass fallback: 1. score only the original rail coordinates, exactly as before, with the added cross-net stroke check 2. only if none is valid, identify the parallel other-net segment touching an original candidate and derive alternatives at the generic visual trace-clearance distance No obstacle `paddingBuffer` is used. The visual-clearance invariant is three trace widths of centerline separation, which leaves two trace widths of whitespace between trace bodies. In the BQ25895 repro, all GND pieces align at `x = -3.27`; CE remains at `x = -3.33`. Their centerlines are `0.06` schematic units apart instead of the previous `0.022001`-unit epsilon-only separation. ## Snapshot scope Only the BQ25895 solver snapshot differs from `main`. repro130 and example02 are byte-identical to their original snapshots. ## Validation - `bun test` — 161 passed, 4 skipped, 0 failed - `bun run build` - linked core schematic snapshots — 327 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed - linked core full suite — 1,327 passed, 31 skipped, 0 failed - `git diff --check` - exact 640×640 solver snapshot render — centerlines are about 1.94 px apart, leaving about 0.94 px of visible background

title: place split vertical rail labels at outward anchor
description: Fixes label placement for split vertical rails to ensure labels are positioned outside the component body and correctly aligned with the furthest trace endpoint.
body:
Builds on #756, which added the original RP2040 reproduction and is now merged.

## What changed

- detects the reproduced distance-split multi-pin `y+` rail after its initial placement falls back to an outward horizontal label
- handles outward fallbacks symmetrically:
  - `x-` on the left side of a chip
  - `x+` on the right side of a chip
- handles paired same-side power rails with opposite requested directions, such as VBAT `y+` above a compact power symbol and GND `y-` below it
- preserves the established outward label column, attaches at the furthest trace endpoint in the requested vertical direction, and emits a short horizontal connector
- expands the RP2040 regression fixture to mirror the rail on both chip sides
- adds a focused five-pin VBAT/GND power-group reproduction matching the reported layout
- updates an existing real-world MCU snapshot containing the same right-side V3V3 pattern

## Root cause

The fallback label is anchored at an MSP endpoint near the middle of the grouped pins. `AvailableNetOrientationSolver` accepts a valid rotation there before considering valid anchors farther along the rail.

Placing directly on the furthest rail endpoint fixes the vertical position but can let the rotated label extend into the chip. The candidate now keeps the furthest rail point as its connector source while preserving the collision-checked outward label column.

The behavior is limited to two explicit shapes: distance-split upward rails with a port-only peer, and opposite-direction multi-pin rails wholly contained on the same side of one chip. This avoids changing ordinary signal labels and unrelated rail arrangements.

## Impact

- V3V3 labels render at the top of split vertical rails on both left and right chip sides.
- Compact same-side VBAT/GND groups place VBAT at the top and GND at the bottom.
- Labels remain fully outside the component body and connect through a short horizontal trace.

## Validation

- visual review of the regenerated symmetric RP2040 SVG snapshot
- visual review of the new compact VBAT/GND SVG snapshot
- real-world right-side MCU snapshot coverage

title: Honor explicit insertion_direction and follow the top/bottom rename
description: Changes the cable insertion point logic to prioritize the explicit insertion direction defined in the component, while also updating deprecated direction names to align with recent changes in Circuit JSON.
body:
## What

`guessCableInsertCenter` always inferred the cable insertion side from pad
geometry, picking whichever side had the largest gap between the pad bounds and
the overall component bounds. That heuristic is a good fallback, but it was used
even when the component already declared the answer.

`pcb_component.insertion_direction` states which side the cable or mating part
is attached from. This PR uses it when present and falls back to the geometric
guess when it is absent, so a connector whose pads happen to sit off-center no
longer gets an insertion point on the wrong side.

## Direction names

Circuit JSON recently renamed `insertion_direction`'s +/-Y values from
`from_front`/`from_back` to `from_top`/`from_bottom`, so that every name is read
off the board as drawn in the 2D PCB view (`top` = +Y, `bottom` = -Y,
`left` = -X, `right` = +X), and added `from_below` (-Z) to pair with
`from_above` (+Z). See tscircuit/circuit-json.

`sideFromInsertionDirection` accepts all three spellings of each direction:

| Direction | Cartesian alias | Deprecated | `CableInsertSide` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from_left` | `from_x_neg` | | `left` |
| `from_right` | `from_x_pos` | | `right` |
| `from_top` | `from_y_pos` | `from_front` | `top` |
| `from_bottom` | `from_y_neg` | `from_back` | `bottom` |
| `from_above` | `from_z_pos` | | `above` |
| `from_below` | `from_z_neg` | | `below` |

The deprecated spellings are still accepted so Circuit JSON produced by an
older core keeps resolving. Circuit JSON normalizes every accepted spelling to
the six named values on parse, so in practice only those six arrive here; the
aliases are accepted for hand-written or unparsed input.

## `CableInsertSide` gains `"below"`

`"above"` already existed for a part mated from +Z. `from_below` had no
counterpart, so it fell through to the geometric guess and produced an
arbitrary *planar* side for a part mated from underneath. `"below"` now returns
the footprint center, exactly as `"above"` does — the insertion point is the
same, only the axis differs.

This widens the exported `CableInsertSide` union, so a consumer doing an
exhaustive `switch` over it will need a `"below"` arm.

## Dependency bump

`tscircuit` moves to `^0.0.2202` alongside `circuit-json` `^0.0.461`. The older
`tscircuit` requires `format-si-unit` `^0.0.3` while the new `circuit-json`
requires `^0.0.7`. Because `^` on a `0.0.x` version pins exactly, the two ranges
are disjoint, so bun resolved `0.0.3` at the root and `circuit-json` failed to
import `parseAndConvertSiUnit`, breaking every test that loads it. `tscircuit`
is a devDependency used by three test files only.

## Testing

`bun test` — 101 pass, 0 fail.

Note `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports pre-existing `Cannot find module 'bun:test'`
errors, unrelated to this change: `tsconfig.json` sets `"types": ["tscircuit"]`,
which excludes `@types/bun`. The repo has no CI workflows.

title: Respect connected pad neck widths
description: Prevents expanded copper from overhanging a connected pads physical cross-section and constrains terminal caps using the largest circle that fits inside the connected pad.
body:
## Summary

- prevent expanded copper from overhanging a connected pad's physical cross-section
- insert a width transition at the pad boundary so the route can still reach its nominal width immediately outside the pad
- constrain terminal caps using the largest circle that fits inside the connected pad
- give the repair pass enough iterations to retain inserted boundary transitions
- add a focused reproduction for the 0.3 mm pad escape seen in autorouter bugreport64
- update the two affected visual/coverage expectations to account for the physically required short necks

This PR is stacked on #10 because the autorouter integration needs both protections: immutable preloaded-copper obstacles and connected-pad width limits.

## Root cause

Same-net pads are intentionally excluded from collision checks, so the expander previously treated the interior of a connected pad as unlimited same-net copper area. A nominal 0.5 mm power trace could therefore be widened to 0.475 mm while still inside a 0.3 mm-tall pad.

The final clearance-repair stage now caps interior route points to the pad width projected normal to the trace direction and caps terminal points to the largest circle that fits inside the pad. When a segment exits a pad, it inserts an explicit transition on the pad boundary rather than narrowing the rest of the route. This also handles a direct pad-to-pad segment by inserting transitions at both pad boundaries.

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 9999999` — 38 pass, 0 fail
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Support immutable fixed trace obstacles
description: Adds support for immutable fixed traces in the power trace expander, allowing preloaded copper to participate in clearance checks without being mutated.
body:
## Summary

- add an explicit `fixedTraces` input for immutable preloaded copper
- include fixed traces and vias in every spatial clearance index without returning or mutating them
- include fixed-trace aliases in connectivity resolution
- reproduce a power trace expanding beside a preloaded signal trace

## Root cause

The expander previously modeled only the traces it was allowed to mutate. Pipeline users with preloaded routing therefore had to either omit that copper from collision checks or include it in the mutable output set. Omitting it allowed newly widened traces and vias to overlap existing board copper.

## Impact

Callers can now pass preloaded routing through `fixedTraces`. It participates in trace, via, and same-net clearance decisions while remaining byte-for-byte outside the solver output.

## Validation

- `bun test` — 37 passed
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build`
- focused immutable-trace collision reproduction

title: Route peripheral plane drops during fanout
description: Updates the autorouting configuration to use fanoutPourNetMap for routing peripheral plane drops, replacing fixed pcbPath entries, and refreshes the PCB snapshot.
body:
## Summary

- update to `tscircuit` 0.0.2200, which includes the merged core fanout-boundary behavior
- replace U2, J1, and J2 manual power/ground `pcbPath` declarations with per-breakout `fanoutPourNetMap` configuration
- route peripheral plane drops during each component's own fanout phase
- refresh the tracked PCB snapshot

## Root cause

The peripheral power and ground traces were pre-routed with fixed `pcbPath` entries. Those routes existed before phased autorouting began, so the phase debugger displayed U2 and J1 geometry during the RK3326 phase. U2's fixed coordinates also placed 20 vias directly in its BGA pads, while J1 and J2 each converged manual paths on component-local coordinates.

Using `fanoutPourNetMap` makes plane drops part of the owning breakout's fanout input. Phase ownership is now:

- RK3326: 224 connections
- U2: 31 connections (11 signals + 20 GND/VCC/VCCQ drops)
- J1: 5 connections (4 signals + GND)
- J2: 16 connections (10 signals + 6 GND drops)
- global route: 25 signal interconnects

## PCB snapshot

![RK3326 PCB snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/rk3326/refs/heads/codex/route-peripheral-plane-drops-in-fanout/__snapshots__/index.circuit-pcb.snap.svg)

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun test tests/rk3326.test.ts` — 10 passed
- `tsci build` with autorouter debugging — all five phases completed with zero autorouter errors
- refreshed `__snapshots__/index.circuit-pcb.snap.svg`

The final DRC currently reports two 0.060 mm trace-clearance errors around J2's D3N/D3P fanout. They are visible for follow-up and are not hidden by this PR.

body:
## Summary

- add a white-and-blue browser-local Altium project viewer by tscircuit
- support folders, loose Altium files, ZIP archives, and public GitHub project URLs
- render schematic sheets, PCB overviews, complete boards, and individual PCB layers as SVG
- deploy the viewer through Vercel at https://altiumviewer.tscircuit.com
- provide privacy messaging and prefilled GitHub bug reports when parsing fails

## TI SPRCAL9 compatibility

The TI SPRCAL9 download is a vendor package containing nested project ZIPs and duplicated design files. The viewer now recursively discovers nested ZIPs with file-count, nesting-depth, and expanded-size limits, avoids inflating irrelevant large artifacts, and deduplicates mirrored Altium documents.

Large PCBs open on a surface-layer overview first while retaining the complete all-layer view. This keeps the 424,275-record TMDS62LEVM board responsive: its overview is about 9 MB and renders in roughly 4 seconds, while the complete all-layer SVG is about 126 MB.

## Root cause fixed

Chrome failed while parsing one 73,111-field copper region because the parser inserted every field through a single spread call, exceeding the browser's argument limit. Fields are now merged iteratively, which preserves parsing behavior without depending on engine-specific stack limits.

## Validation

- uploaded the exact `sprcal9.zip` to the deployed production viewer
- confirmed 57 schematic sheets and one 1,585-component PCB
- confirmed the 424,275-record PCB overview renders locally in Chrome

body:
## Summary

- add 20 breadboard-friendly header modules with idiomatic TSX components and per-module PCB/schematic snapshots
- use the dedicated `headermodule` footprint name for pluggable board modules while preserving `pinrow` for ordinary headers
- normalize common power pin identifiers so renders remain valid (`3.3V` -> `V3_3`, `+3V3` -> `V3_3`, `+5V` -> `V5`)
- assert that each snapshot test creates no source component errors, preventing black/empty footprint snapshots from being accepted
- style header-module footprints with a rectangular silkscreen border, concise per-pin PCB labels, and a short module title such as `XIAO RP2040`

## Why

tscircuit pin identifiers support letters, numbers, and underscores. The previous power labels containing `+` or `.` were filtered out by core, which could leave a component creation error behind and produce an empty/black render. The module metadata still uses the real voltage values (`3.3V` and `5V`); only the pin identifiers are normalized.

The corresponding core warning/error guidance is in [tscircuit/core#2976](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/2976).

The `headermodule`, independent-row/sparse-grid, and silkscreen styling syntax is implemented in [tscircuit/footprinter#761](https://github.com/tscircuit/footprinter/pull/761), and core preserves literal custom silkscreen labels in [tscircuit/core#2980](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/2980).

## Verification

title: Fix permutation-aware routing for RK3326 buses
description: Fixes routing issues for RK3326 buses by implementing permutation-aware routing, ensuring proper trace spacing and avoiding violations during layer changes.
body:
## Summary

- route small buses using canonical spatial lane ranks when terminal arrays require a permutation
- use mitered offset corners and staggered two-dimensional via fields to preserve trace spacing through bends and layer changes
- add outgoing via escape guards and dense fanout turn staggering so buses avoid pads, sibling vias, and nearby copper
- retain the established shared-guard strategy for larger dataset buses
- convert RK3326-03 and RK3326-04 from expected failures into positive SVG, crossing, via-count, keepout, and Circuit JSON DRC tests

## Root cause

The connection array order is not always the physical lane order at each fanout. The detailed router previously applied connection-index offsets directly and used a chord-normal corner offset, which could swap lanes, pinch spacing at bends, or place layer-change fanouts through neighboring vias and pads.

## Impact

RK3326-03 now routes four USB OTG traces with one via per trace. RK3326-04 now routes ten MIPI DSI traces with two vias per trace. Both have zero same-layer crossings, uniform via counts, no keepout violations, and no `@tscircuit/checks` DRC errors.

Existing RK3326-01/02 cases and all ten `dataset-srj12-bus-routing` samples remain passing.

## Validation

- `bun test --timeout 120000` — 25 passed, 0 failed, 170 assertions
- all ten dataset Circuit JSON DRC tests pass
- `bun run build`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build:site`
